Habit, s. Dress, q. v. 2 SIlaM, BAvaH, pra-kfti f., sTiti f., vftti f., avasTA, daSA, svaBAvaH. 3 aByAsaH, nityapravftti f., AcAraH, nityakriyA, vyavahAraH, rIti f., pracAraH, kramaH, Avftti f., anuSIlanaM; ‘in the h(abit) of’ SIla or vftti in comp.; ‘in the h(abit) of stealing’ cOryavftti; mfgayASIla, &c.; ‘bad h(abit)’ vya-sanaM, durguRaH; ‘having bad h(abit)s’ durvftta, durA-cAra, pApavftti, Brazwacaritra. v. t. Dress, q. v. [Habit]able, a. vAsakzama, vasatiyogya. [Habit]ation, s. vAsaH, DAman n., vasati f., AlayaH, gfhaM, gehaM, AgAraM; See House. [Habit]ual, a. aByAsaja, nitya, satata, anuSIlita, AByAsika-vyAvahArika-svABAvika (kI f.); ‘a h(abitual) drunkard’ nityapAnAsaktaH; ‘a h(abitual) worker’ kriyAvAn, karmasu udyataH kArmaH, karmaSIlaH. [Habit]ually, adv. nityaM, satataM, yaTAByAsaM, yaTArIti, yaTAvyava-hAraM. [Habit]uate, v. t. aByas 4 U, anuSIl 10, Sikz c., parici c., aByasta-paricita a. kf 8 U; ‘h(abituat)ed to distress’ jYAtaduHKa, paricitakleSa; duHKaSIla, duHKABijYa.
HABIT: I Dress: q.v.: veSaH.II Condition, temperament: q.v.: avasTA.III Practice, custom:(1) aByAsaH (?);(2) SIlam (?), of bad h. s: aSIlaH (lA, laM), Ki. To be in the h. of: SIlaH (lA, laM) in comp.

HABIT , s. (Dress) veSaH, vezaH, vasanaM, vastraM, vAsas n., pariDAnaM, paricCadaH, sambaraM. — (State, condition) avasTA, sTitiH f., BAvaH, vfttiH f., daSA, saMsTitiH f., svaBAvaH; ‘habit of body,’ SarIrasTitiH f., dehasvaBAvaH; ‘habit of mind,’ cittavfttiH f. — (Temperament, disposition) prakftiH f., SIlaH -latA, svaBAvaH, antaHkaraRaM. — (Custom, practice, established manner) AcAraH, aByAsaH, vyavahAraH, samAcAraH, nityakftyaM, nityakriyA, rItiH f., vyavahftiH f., SIlaH, pracAraH, caritaM, caryyA, kramaH, niyamaH, AvfttiH f., vyApAraH, pravfttiH f., mArgaH, anuSIlanaM; ‘bad habit,’ vyasanaM; ‘having bad habits,’ durAcAraH -rA -raM, pApa- samAcAraH -rA -raM, pApacaryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, durvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, duScaritraH -trA -traM, vyasanI -ninI -ni (n).
To HABIT , v. a. vezw (c. 1. vezwate -zwituM), parivezw, ACad (c. 10. -CAda- yati -yituM), vastra (nom. vastrayati -yituM), pariDA in caus. (-DApayati -yituM).
HABITABLE: vAsayogyaH (gyA, gyaM): v. Inhabi- -table.

HABITANT: nivAsin (f. nI): v. Inhabi- -tant.
HABITANT , s. vAsI m. (n), nivAsI m., nilAyI m. (n), vAsakft.
HABITATION: (1) vasatiH, the h. of serpents: BujaNga- mAnAM vasatiH, R.;(2) DAman (n.), the h. of gods: tridaSaDAma, N.: v. Residence, house.

HABITATION , s. vAsaH, vAsasTAnaM, nivAsaH, vasatiH f., nivasatiH f., gfhaM, gehaH -haM, veSma m. (n), nilayaH -yanaM, AlayaH, AyatanaM, niveSanaM, niketaH -tanaM, AgAraH, BavanaM, vasitaM, samAvAsaH, avasTAnaM, AvasaTaH, sTAnaM, okas n., DAma n. (n).
HABITUAL: (1) nitya (f. tyA) (= every day); (2) aByAsajaH (jA, jaM) (formed by habit) (?).

HABITUAL , a. AByAsikaH -kI -kaM, aByastaH -stA -staM, AcArikaH -kI -kaM, AcaritaH -tA -taM, vyAvahArikaH -kI -kaM, vyavahArikaH -kI -kaM, nityaH -tyA -tyaM, svABAvikaH -kI -kaM, anuSIlitaH -tA -taM, nEyamikaH -kI -kaM, prAyikaH -kI -kaM.
HABITUALLY: (1) nityam;(2) satatam (= const- -antly).
HABITUALLY , adv. nityaM, nityaSas, yaTAvyavahAra, yaTArIti, sAByAsaM, aByAsena, aByAsapUrvvaM, yaTAByAsaM.
HABITUALLY , adv. sadA or SIla or nitya in comp.; ‘habitually dejected,’ sadAvizAdI -dinI &c., nityavizAdI &c.; ‘silent,’ tUzRIMSIlaH -lA -laM.
HABITUATE: aByAsaM karoti: v. To accustom.
To HABITUATE , v. a. aByas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM), aByAsaM kf, aByastaM -stAM -staM kf, Sikz (c. 10. Sikzayati -yituM), SIl (c. 10. SIlayati -yituM); ‘to be habituated,’ aByastaH -stA -staM BU.
HABITUATED , p. p. aByastaH -stA -staM, SikzitaH -tA -taM, kftAByAsaH -sA -saM, SIlitaH -tA -taM, anuSIlitaH -tA -taM, SIlaH -lA -laM in comp.
HABITUDE: I Familiarity: q.v.II Mode: prakAraH (?)
HABITUDE , s. (Custom) vyavahAraH, AcAraH, rItiH f., caritaM, caryyA, nityakftyaM. — (Relation) sambanDaH, samparkaH, pratIkzA. — (Intercourse) saMsargaH.

Hack, v. t. KaMqaSaH kft 6 P or Cid 7 P, pahulavaSaH vraSc 6 P or vidF 10, vyavacCid. s. prahAraH, CedaH, AGAtaH. 2 paRyASvaH, kadaSvaH, jIrRaH aSvaH, sarvaprayojyaH-sarvasADAraRaH-aSvaH. 3 hInavfttiH, nIcakarmakArin m. vrAtInaH, sarvaprayojyaH, paRyaH.
HACK (subs.): I A cut: q.v.:II A procuress: q.v.III A horse for hire: BAwakaGowakaH (?).
HACK (v.): vyava-Cinatti (Cid, c. 7.): v. Cut to pieces.

To HACK , v. a. (Mangle) vyavaCid (c. 7. -Cinatti -CettuM), vraSc (c. 6. vfScati, vraScituM), pravraSc, vidF (c. 10. -dArayati -yituM), bahulavaSaH KaRq (c. 10. KaRqayati -yituM) or Cid, bahuKaRqaSaH kf, KaRqaM KaRqaM kf, bahuKa- RqIkf, kzatavikzatIkf.
To HACK , v. n. (For hire) atiSarIrAyAsena nIcakarmma kf, nirantarA- yAsaM kf, paRyaH -RyA -RyaM BU, sarvvaprayojyaH -jyA -jyaM BU, sarvvasADAraRIBU.

HACK , s. (Cut) prahAraH, CedaH, AGAtaH, CurikAGAtaH. — (Horse kept for hire, worn out horse) kadaSvaH, paRyASvaH, BAwakIyavAjI m. (n), sADAraRavAjI m., sarvvaprayojyavAjI m., paRyaGowakaH, aSvakaH; ‘hack-carriage,’ paRyavAhanaM, sADAraRaraTaH. — (Drudge) nirantarA- yAsI m. (n), atidehakleSena nIcakarmmakArI m. (n), hInavfttiH m., vrAtInaH.
HACKED , p. p. vyavaCinnaH -nnA -nnaM, kzatavikzataH -tA -taM, vfkRaH -kRA -kRaM.
Hackle, s. umAmArjanI-SoDanI.
To HACKLE , v. a. vakzyamARayantreRa SaRaM or atasIM mfj (c. 2. mArzwi -rzwuM) or sammfj, or parizkf or SuD (c. 10. SoDayati -yituM) or pfTakkf.
HACKLE , s. atasImArjanI, SaRamArjakaH, umASoDanI.

HACKNEY , s. (Horse) kadaSvaH, aSvakaH, paRyASvaH, paRyaGowakaH, sADAra- RavAjI m. (n), BAwakIyavAjI m. — (Any thing much used, a drudge, a hireling) nIcakarmmaRi niyuktaMH, nIcakarmmakArI m. (n), nirantarAyAsI m. (n), hInavfttiH m., vEtanikaH, paRyaH, sADAraRaH, sarvvaprayojyaH. — (Prostitute) paRyastrI, sADAraRastrI.
To HACKNEY , v. a. nIcakarmmaRi niyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM, c. 10. -yoja- yati -yituM), paRyIkf, sADAraRIkf, sarvvaprayojyaM -jyAM, jyaM kf, jIrRIkf.
HACKNEY-COACH: BAwakayAnam (?); gen. simp. yAnam.

HACKNEYED (adj.): (1) sADAraRa (f. RI) (= com- -mon);(2) jIrRa (f. rRA) (= worn out);(3) bahuBiH praRItaH (tA, taM) (of subjects), Ana; (4) bahuprayuktaH (ktA, ktaM) (of words, etc.).
HACKNEYED , p. p. sarvvaprayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, sarvvasADAraRaH -RA -RI -RaM, sarvvapaRyaH -RyA -RyaM, apakarmmaniyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, jIrRaH -rRA -rRaM.

HADES , s. pretalokaH, aDolokaH, aDoBuvanaM, narakaH, pAtAlaM.

HAGGISH , a. kurUpiRI, aparUpiRI, virUpiRI, jarApariRatA.
Haggle, v. i. krayavikrayakAle vilaMb 1 A or vivad 1 A.
HAGGLE (v.): perh. kalahaM karoti.

HAGIOGRAPHA , s. DarmmagranTaH, DarmmaSAstrasaMhitA, DarmmapustakaM.
Hagiology, sidDacaritraleKaH.
HAH: AH: v. Oh.
HAH , interj. hA, aho, ahovat, ahaha, hAhA, A, ayi, AScaryyaM.

Hail, interj. namaH, svasti, (with dat.); oft. ex. by ji 1 P; jayatu jayatu devaH ‘h(ail) to Your Majesty’; kuSalaM BUyAt, aBi-vAdaye. s. SilAvfzwi f., karakAnipAtaH; ‘h(ail)-stone’ karakA varzopalaH, varzaSilA, payo-GanaH, Gana-meGa-kaPaH; ‘h(ail)-storm’ karakAsAraH, SilAvarzaH. v. i. upalAn vfz 1 P or nipat c., karakAsAraM pat c. v. t. vaMd 1 A, aBivad 10 A, saMbuD c., AmaMtr 10 A, A-aBi-BAz 1 A, A-hve 1 P. 2 (fig.) prItyA-mudA-aMgIkf 8 U; aBinaMd 1 P.
HAIL (interj.): namaH (with dat.) “SiKine'neka- SiKAya te namaH”, Ki.
HAIL (subs.): (1) SilAvfzwiH;(2) karakAvfzwiH, heavy h.: tumulakarakAvfzwiH, Me. i. 55. H. water: karakA- jalam, Bha.
HAIL (v.): I To salute: q.v.: vandate (vand, c. 1.).II Of h.: expr. by subs. or varzati, it h. ed heavily burning firebrands: jvaladBiraNgAra- cayErnaBastalaM vavarza gAQam, Ku.

HAIL , s. (Frozen rain) karakA, karakAvfzwiH f., SilA, SilAvfzwiH f. varzopalaH, payoGanaH, payogaqaH, GanakaPaH, meGAsTi n., meGakaPaH, meGagarBaH, DArA, toyaqimBaH, marutPalaM, piRqABraM, DArANkuraH, mawatI, SilInDraM, vArzilA.
HAIL , exclam. namas, svasti, kuSalaM, kuSalaM BUyAt, suKaM BUyAt, kalyARaM BUyAt, kzemaM Bavatu, SevaM, aBivAdaye, aBivande.
To HAIL , v. n. (Pour down hail) karakAsAraM vfz (c. 1. varzati -rzituM), SilA vfz, upalAn vfz or pat (c. 10. pAtayati -yituM).

To HAIL , v. a. (Call from a distance) dUrAd Ahve (c. 1. -hvayati -hvAtuM) or hve or samboDanaM kf or Akrand (c. 1. -krandati -ndituM) or Amantr (c. 10. -mantrayate -yituM) or samAmantr or aBiBAz (c. 1. -BAzate -zituM) or ABAz. — (Salute) vand (c. 1. vandate -ndituM), aBivand, aBivad (c. 10. -vAdayati -te -yituM), namaskf, Amantr, upAs (c. 2. -Aste -AsituM).
HAIL-STONE , s. SilA, varzopalaH, payoGanaH, karakA, payogaqaH
HAIL-STORM , s. karakAsAraH, karakAvfzwiH f., SilAsAraH.
HAILED , p. p. dUrAd AhUtaH -tA -taM or aBihitaH -tA -taM or AmantritaH -tA -taM, samboDitaH -tA -taM, AkranditaH -tA -taM.
HAILSTONE: (1) karakA;(2) varzopalaH and sim. comp.s.
HAILY: expr. by comp., h. shower: karakAvfzwiH.
HAILY , a. karakAmayaH -yI -yaM, SilAmayaH -yI -yaM, varzopalamayaH &c.

Hair, s. keSaH, kacaH, bAlaH, cikuraH, kuMtalaH; ‘h(air) on the head’ SiroruhaH, mUrDajaH, Sira-sijaH. 2 (Of the body gen.) ro(lo)-mana n., tanUruhaH-haM, tanujaH; ‘quantity of h(air)’ kESyaM, kESika. 3 keSa(sa)raH; ‘whole collection of h(air)’ keSakalApaH-pakzaH-hastaH-pASaH; ‘h(air) hanging on the forehead’ BramarakAH; ‘lock of h(air)’ kAkapakzaH, SiKaMqakaH; ‘matted h(air)’ jawA, sawA; ‘a braid of h(air)’ kabarI, keSaveSaH; ‘curled h(air)’ alakaH, cUrRa-kuMtalaH; ‘braided h(air)’ veRi-RI f., Da-mmillaH; ‘crest-h(air)’ SiKA, cUqA, keSapASI; ‘clean h(air)’ SIrzaRyaH, SirasyaH, ‘h(air)-broom or brush’ keSamArjanI-SoDanI; ‘h(air)-dressing’ keSaracanA-saMskAraH; ‘even a h(air)s breadth’, reKAmAtramapi; ‘a h(air)-breadth escape’ kaTamapi labDA muktiH. [Hair]less, a. akeSa, keSahIna, vikeSa. [Hair]y, a. lomaSa, lomAvfta pracura-bahu-loman, lomamaya (yI f.), lomavat, lomapUrRa, keSava, keSin, keSika.

HAIR: I Of the head:(1) keSaH, seizing by the h.: keSErgfhItvA, P.; here they are dressing the h. of horses: ito'SvAnAM keSakalpanA kriyate, Mr. iv.; the Śakas with short h, the Pāradas with flowing h.: ardDamuRqAn SakAn, pralambakeSAn pAradAn, V.p. iv. 3.; arranging the h. in the folds of a peacock's tail: mayUrabarhiBaNgyA keSpASaM viDAya, D.;(2) kacaH; (3) kuntalaH;(4) cikfraH;(5) SiroruhaH, mUrdDajaH, etc. (poet). The entire h. of the head:(1) keSapASaH; (2) keSakalApaH;(3) kacOGaH, N.;(4) cikuraprakaraH. N.; etc., (her) h. not very curly, thick, long and every one of them naturally equal, smooth, and black: anatiBaNguro bahula AyAmavAnekEkanisargasama- snigDanIlo mUrdDajakalApaH, D. vi. Matted or clotted h.: jawA, -juwaH; Curly h.:(1) alakaH;(2) cUrRakuntalaH. H.; twisted together into a single braid: veRiH (RI); to do so: veRIM or SiKAM baDnAti, Me. A braid of h.: kavarI. Ornamental h.: DamBillaH (rare.) [Page331] II Of the body:(1) ri(lo)man (n.), with gladdened h.: hfzwaroman (mfn.), Ram.;(2) bAlaH (specially of an animal's tail), Ki.;(3) tanu(nU)ruham (poet).III Of plants: keSa(sa)raH, Ph.: a h.'s breadth: reKAmAtramapi, R.

HAIR , s. keSaH, bAlaH, kacaH, cikuraH, vfjanaH -jinaH, kuntalaH. — (Of the head) keSaH, SiroruhaH, Siroruw m., SirasijaH, mUrdDajaH, kfSalA. — (Of the body) loma n. (n), roma n. (n), tanuruhaH -haM, tanUruhaH -haM, tanuruw m. (h), tanujaM, aNkuraH; ‘a head of hair,’ kESyaM, kESikaM; ‘a quantity of hair,’ keSakalApaH, keSapakzaH, keSoccayaH, keSapASaH, kacapASaH, kacapakzaH, kacahastaH, cikurapASaH, cikurapakzaH, cikurahastaH; ‘having much or fine hair,’ keSI -SinI -Si (n), keSavAn -vatI -vat (t), keSavaH -vA -vaM, keSikaH -kI -kaM; ‘a fine head [Page328-a+ 51] of hair,’ keSaBAraH, kavarIBAraH -BaraH; ‘a braid of hair,’ kavarI, keSagarBaH -rBakaH, keSaveSaH; ‘braided hair,’ DammillaH, veRiH -RI f., veRikA, praveRiH -RI f.; ‘a lock of hair,’ alakaH -kaM, cUrRakuntalaH, BramarakaH, kAkapakzaH, SiKaRqaH -RqakaH, keSapASI, cUqA, SiKA; ‘clotted hair,’ jawA, sawA; ‘unentangled hair,’ SIrzaRyaH, SirasyaH; ‘covered with hair,’ lomaSaH -SA -SaM, bahulomA -mA -ma (n), romA- krAntaH -ntA -ntaM; ‘point of hair,’ bAlAgraM; ‘erection of the hair,’ romaharzaRaM, udDarzaRaM. See ERECTION. — (Filament of a plant) keSaraH, kesaraH.

HAIR-BRUSH , s. keSamArjanI, keSaSoDanI, keSanirGarzaRakaH.
HAIR-CLOTH , s. lomanirmmitaM vastraM, keSamayaH pawaH.
HAIR-CUTTER , s. keSaCid m. -CettA m. (ttf), SiroruhaCedakaH.
HAIR-DRESSER , s. keSaracakaH, keSaviracakaH, keSasaMskArakft m.
HAIR-DRESSING , s. keSaracanA, keSaviracanaM -nA, keSasaMskAraH.
HAIR-POWDER: keSacUrRam (?).
HAIR-SPRING: *keSAgratAraH; sUkzmatAraH.
HAIRCLOTH: lo(ro)mapawaH (??).
HAIRDRESSER: keSakalpakaH: v. Barber.
HAIRED , a. keSI -SinI -Si (n), keSavAn -vatI -vat (t).
HAIRINESS: lo(ro)maSatA, -tvam: v. Hairy.

Half, a. arDa, sAmi in comp.; ‘h(alf) done’ sAmikftaM. s. arDaH-rDaM, arDaBAgaH, arDAMSaH; in comp. ex. by arDa; arDAMgaM, pUrvArDaH, &c.; ‘a year and a h(alf)’ sArDavatsaraH; ‘h(alf) eaten’ arDaBukta; arDavivfta, arDacCinna, &c.; ‘h(alf)-brother’ vEmAtreyaH, sApatnaH, anyo-daryaMHdaryaH, vEmAtraH; ‘h(alf)-blood’ Binnodara, Binna-garBa, anyodarya; ‘h(alf)-dead’ mftakalpa-prAya, maraRonmuKa, Asannamftyu, mumUrzu, kaMWagataprARa; ‘h(alf)-hearted’ nirutsAha, utsAhahIna, AsTA-rahita; ‘h(alf) moon’ arDeduHarDeMduH, caMdrArDaH; ‘h(alf)-sister’ vEmAtreyI, vEmAtrI, anyodaryA; ‘h(alf)-starved’ kzuDAvasannaprAya, kzutkzAmakalpa; ‘h(alf) way’ arDamArge-paTe, maDyamArge; ‘h(alf) year’ arDavarzaM; ‘h(alf) yearly’ zARmAsika-ArDavArzika (kI f.); ‘h(alf) a bread is better than no loaf’ sarvanASe samutpanne arDaM tyajati paMqitaH or arDena kurute kAryaM.

HALF (subs.): (1) ardDam, h. the day is over: ardDaM gataM divasasya, V.; will take the other h.: aparamardDaM gfhRIyuH, Da.; and its h. in width: tadarDena tu vistftA, A. p.;(2) ardDaBagaH or arDAMSaH, with h. of it: tadardDa- BAgena, Ku. Ph.: in h., i.e. in two: dviDA; each of them went halves with her: ardDArdDaBAgAByAM tAmayojayatAmuBe, R. x. 56.

HALF , s. ardDaM -rdDaH, ardDaBAgaH, ardDAMSaH; ‘half an hour,’ ardDadaRqaH; ‘half a league,’ ardDakroSaH; ‘half a hundred,’ ardDaSataM; ‘half the body,’ ardDANgaM; ‘a year and a half,’ sArdDavatsaraH; ‘a hun- dred and a half,’ sArdDaSataM; ‘the best half,’ uttamArdDaM -rdDyaM; ‘the last half,’ avarArdDaM, paScArdDaM; ‘sharing a half,’ ardDaBAgI -ginI -gi (n), ardDAMSI -SinI -Si (n), ardDI -rdDinI -rdDi (n); ‘lasting half a month,’ ArdDamAsikaH -kI -kaM.
HALF , a. ardDaH -rdDA -rdDaM, ArdDikaH -kI -kaM, ardDikaH -kA -kaM; ‘half assent,’ ardDANgIkAraH; ‘half moon,’ ardDacandraH.

HALF , adv. ardDaM, ardDena, sAmi; ‘half-man, half-woman,’ ardDena puruzo'rdDena strI; ‘half-eaten,’ ardDaBuktaH -ktA -ktaM, jagDArdDaH -rdDA -rdDaM, sAmiBuktaH -ktA -ktaM; ‘half-drank,’ ardDapItaH -tA -taM, sAmipItaH -tA -taM; ‘half-read,’ ardDavAcitaH -tA -taM; ‘half-spoken,’ ardDoktaH -ktA -ktaM; ‘half-closed,’ ardDasaMvftaH -tA -taM, mukulitaH -tA -taM, nimI- litaH -tA -taM.
HALF , (With numerals); ‘Thirteen and a half,’ sArdDatrayodaSa.
HALF-AFRAID: BItaBItaH (tA, taM), Ki. xiv. 65.
HALF-BINDING: ardDacarmabanDanam (?).
HALF-BLOOD , s. or a. BinnodaraH -rA -raM, BinnanABiH -BiH -Bi, BinnagarBaH -rBA -rBaM, asamAnodaraH -rA -raM, BinnodaryyaH, anyodaryyaH, BinnaSarIrAnvayaH.
HALF-BOOT: *AgulPapAdukA.
HALF-BRED: ardDaSikzitaH (tA, taM) (?) (used in Bengali).

HALF-BROTHER , s. vEmAtraH -treyaH, BrAtA dvEmAturaH, anyodaryyaH, sApatnaH.
HALF-BURNT: (1) ardDadagDa (f. gDA) and sim. comp.s.;(2) dagDAdagDa (f. gDA), D.
HALF-CASTE: saNkIrRayoni (mfn.), M. x. 25.
HALF-COOKED: ardDasidDaH (dDA, dDaM).
HALF-DEAD: (1) ardDamftaH (tA, taM);(2) mftakalpaH (lpA, lpaM);(3) mftaprAyaH (yA, yaM).

HALF-DOZENTH: zazWa (f. zWI): v. Sixth.
HALF-EATEN: ardDopaBuktaH (ktA, ktaM), Ku. and sim. comp.s.

HALF-HOLIDAY: in schools; perh. ardDAnaDyAyaH.
HALF-HOLIDAY , s. ardDotsavaH, ardDamahotsavaH, ardDAnaDyAyaH.
HALF-LEARNED , a. alpajYAnI -ninI -ni (n), kiYcijjYaH -jjYA -jjYaM, cumbakaH.
HALF-LOST , a. nazwaprAyaH -yA -yaM, AsannanASaH -SA -SaM, nASonmuKaH -KI -KaM.
HALF-MOON , s. ardDacandraH, candrArdDaM, ardDenduH m.; ‘shaped like a half- moon,’ ardDacandrAkAraH -rA -raM, ardDacandrAkftiH -tiH -ti.

HALF-SEAS-OVER: (1) ardDamattaH (ttA, taM);(2) maDyena madena mattaH (ttA, ttaM), Ni.

HALF-UTTERED , a. ardDoktaH -ktA -ktaM, ardDoditaH -tA -taM, ardDakaTitaH -tA -taM.

HALF-WITTED , a. alpabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, alpaDIH -DIH -Di, alpameDAH -DAH -DaH (s).
HALF-YEAR: (1) zaRmAsaH;(2) ardDavarzaH and sim. comp.s.

HALF-YEARLY: I Adj.:(1) zARmAsikaH (kI, kaM);(2) ardDavArzikaH (kI, kaM);II Adv.: zaRmAse zaRmAse, M.

HALL: (1) SAlA;(2) saBA (= public h.), the h. of Brahmā is not supported by columns: brAhmI saBA stammErna DftA, Mah.;(3) cEtyam, -kam (= religious h. of Buddhists), Mah. ii. 21. 19.

HALLELUJAH: ISvaragItam (?).

Hallow, v. t. pavitrIkf 8 U, pUj 10, mah 1 P, 10, arc 1 P, 10. 2 saMskf, prokz 1 P, aBizic 6 P.

(Make holy) pavitrIkf, pavitraM -trAM -traM kf, puRyIkf, puRyaM -RyAM -RyaM kf, pUjyaM -jyAM -jyaM kf, SudDIkf. — (Consecrate) saMskf, aBisaMskf, aBizic (c. 6. -ziYcati -zektuM), prokz (c. 1. -ukzati -kzituM), pratizWA in caus. (-zWApayati -yituM), DarmmArTaM viniyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM) or nirdiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM).

(Made holy, reverenced) pavitrIkftaH -tA -taM, pavitritaH -tA -taM, pUjitaH -tA -taM, pUjyaH -jyA -jyaM, arcitaH -tA -taM — (Consecrated) saMskftaH -tA -taM, kftasaMskAraH -rA -raM, pratizWitaH -tA -taM. supratizWitaH -tA -taM, prokzitaH -tA -taM, praRItaH -tA -taM, aBiziktaH -ktA [Page329-a+ 51] -ktaM, DarmmArTaM viniyojitaH -tA -taM.

HALM , s. (Straw) tfRaM, palAlaH -laM -lI, palaH, DAnyakalkaM.

HALO , s. dyutimAlA, aMSumAlA, sUryyaparigataM or candraparigataM dyutimaRqalaM or dIptimaRqalaM or raktavarRamaRqalaM, dIpticakraM, dyutivalayaH, pariDiH m., pariveSaH.
Halser, s. nOguRaH-rajju f.
HALSER , s. nOrajjuH m., nOguRaH, nObanDanarajjuH, nObanDanArTaM mahAguRaH.

Halt, v. i. niviS 6 P, avasTA 1 A, prayARaBaMgaM kf 8 U, aDvamaDye sTA. 2 viram 1 P, viSram 4 P. 3 laMg 1 P. a. paMgu, gati-vikala, SroRa. s. niveSaH, avasTiti f., avasTAnaM, prayARaBaMgaH, yAnanivftti-virati f.; viSrAmaH; ‘h(alt)ing place’ niveSasTAnaM. 2 laMganaM.

HALT , a. (Lame) paNguH -NguH -Ngu, KaYjaH -YjA -YjaM, KoraH -rA -raM, gativikalaH -lA -laM, pAdavikalaH -lA -laM.

HALTED , p. p. nivfttayAnaH -nA -naM, avasTitaH -tA -taM, sannizaRRaH -RRA -RRaM.

(= to fasten: q.v.), hung banners: DvajAn babanDuH, B. iii. 5.II To kill by h. ing: udvaDnAti (banD, c. 9.), he h. s him- self: ayamAtmAnamudvaDnAti, Mu. vi.; here I will kill myself. h. ing on this Aśoka tree with this creeper: tadihEvASokapAdape'nayA latayodvaDyAtmAnaM vyApA- dayizyAmi, Ra. vii.III To lower: q.v.: namayati (c. of nam).IV To cover, adorn: q.v.: CAdayati (Cad, c. 10).

HANG (v. i.): I Lit.:(1) lambate, pra-, (lamba, c. 1.) (= to dangle; h. down);(2) plavate (pla, c. 1.) (= to float);(3) tizWati (sTA, c. 1.) (=to stay).II To h. on, to stick: sajjate, A-, (saYj, c. 1.), my heart h. s on her: Asajjate me hfdayamasyAm, D. vi.III To h. on or upon, to depend: avalambate, this action h. s on Chārudatta: vyavahAro'yaM cArudattamavalaBbate, Mr. ix.IV To h. to, to cling: q.v.: sajjate.V To h. over, impend:(1) unnamati (nam, c. 1.) (= to rise); (2) better by upari.VI To h. back, to be in suspense: dolAyate (nomi.): v. Also to hesitate, decline.

[Hard]en, v. t. kaWinIkf 8 U, dfQIkf, GanIkf, kf with (a.). [Hard]ly, adv. kaTaM kaTamapi, kazwena, duHKena, kazwaM, kfcCreRa, nEva. [Hard]ness, s. kAWinyaM, dfQatA, kaWoratA, nizWuratA, durboDatA, duzkaratvaM, ugratA, &c. [Hard]ship, s. kazwaH-zwaM, kleSaH, duHKaM, pIqA, bADA, kAya-deha-kleSaH; kfcCraM, AyAsaH, KedaH. Hardy, a. sAhasin, pragalBa, SUra, vIra, DIra, nirBaya, pratiBAnavat, sAhasika (kI f.), vikrAMta, niHSaMka. 2 dfQa or kaWina-deha-SarIra-kAya; ‘of a h(ardy) frame’ siMhasaMhanana; vajradeha. [Hardy]hood, s. vIryaM, SOryaM, sAhasikatA, prAgalByaM, sAhasaM; DfzwatA, pratiBA, nirlajjatA. [Hardy]ness, s. SOryaM, vIryaM, dehakAWinyaM.

HARD (adj.): I To the touch:(1) kaWinaH (nA, naM) (best equiv.), with h. limbs: kaWinEH SarIrEH;(2) kaWoraH, h. er than adamant: vajrAdapi kaWorARi, U.II Fig.: hard-hearted: q.v.: kaWinaH (nA, naM).III Difficult: q.v.:(1) kaWinaH (nA, naM), sometimes they are ambiguous and h.: kvacidvakratA kaWinatA ca, Pra.;(2) kaWoraH (rA, raM), with h. argumentative discourses: kaWoratArkikAlApEH. IV Trying, distressing:(1) kaWinaH (nA, naM), very h. pain: nitAntakaWinAM rujam,V ii.;(2) dInaH (nA, naM): v. Pitiable, wretched.V =exces- -sive: q.v.VI Of wines: perh. karkaSaH (SA, SaM).

HARD (adj.): I Diligently: q.v.: AyAsena. H.-fought battle: BIzaRaM or GoraM yudDam.II With difficulty: q.v.: kazwena. He is h. up for money: DanABAvena kliSyati.III Excessively: q.v.: nitAntam. To drink h.: atipAnaM karoti; h. by: ati- sannihitaH (tA, taM).IV Rapidly: q.v.: SIGram.

HARD , a. (Firm, solid, compact) dfQaH -QA -QaM, GanaH -nA -naM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, kaWoraH -rA -raM, saMhataH -tA -taM, aSiTilaH -lA -laM, amasfRaH -RA -RaM, vajraH -jrA -jraM, grAvA -vA -va (n), vajramayaH -yI -yaM, dfQasanDiH -nDiH -nDi, karkaraH -rA -raM, jaraWaH -WA -WaM, gAQaH -QA -QaM, pragAQaH -QA -QaM, kIkasaH -sA -saM, kakKawaH -wA -waM, kawolaH -lA -laM, krUraH -rA -raM, nizWuraH -rA -raM, dravetaraH -rA -raM. — (Hard to be understood) durjYeyaH -yA -yaM. — (Difficult, not easy to be done) kaWinaH -nA -naM, duzkaraH -rA -rI -raM, duHsADyaH -DyA -DyaM, duScaraH -rA -raM, asukaraH -rI -raM, asugamaH -mA -maM, vizamaH -mA -maM, kazwaH -zwA -zwaM, [Page332-a+ 51] durnivahaH -hA -haM, AyAsakftaH -tA -taM, duHKasADyaH -DyA -DyaM, duHKena kAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM or sADyaH -DyA -DyaM. Often expressed by dur or duHKa in comp.; as, ‘hard to be borne,’ duHsahaH -hA -haM; ‘hard to obtain,’ durlaBaH -BA -BaM, duHKalaByaH -ByA -ByaM, duzprApaH -pA -paM, duHKena prAzyaH -zyA -zyaM; ‘hard to be crossed,’ dustaraH -rA -raM, dustAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM; ‘hard to be broken,’ durBedyaH -dyA -dyaM, duHKaBedyaH -dyA -dyaM; ‘hard to be relinquished,’ dustyajaH -jA -jaM. — (Fatiguing, painful, laborious) kazwakaraH -rI -raM, duHKI -KinI -Ki (n), duHKakaraH -rA -raM, kleSI -SinI -Si (n), kleSakaH -kA -kaM. — (Severe, harsh) kaWoraH -rA -raM, nizWuraH -rA -raM, ugraH -grA -graM, ugradaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, tIkzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, krUraH -rA -raM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, rUkzaH -kzA -kzaM. — (Unfavor- able) ananukUlaH -lA -laM; ‘hard fate,’ durdEvaM. — (Sour, acid) amlarasaH -sA -saM, SuktaH -ktA -ktaM.

HARD , adv. (Near, hard by) samIpaM, nikawe, upAnte, ArAt, AsannaH -nnA -nnaM, sannikfzwaH -zwA -zwaM. — (With difficulty) duHKena, kazwena, kfcCreRa, AyAsena, kaWinaM, vizamaM, dur prefixed. (Violently, with force) balena, balAt, balavat, tIvraM, tIkzRaM, prasaBaM. — (Hard) SIGraM, satvaraM, tvaritaM.

To HARDEN , v. a. kaWinIkf, GanIkf, kaWorIkf, dfQIkf, karkaSIkf, stabDIkf, kaWinaM -nAM -naM kf.
To HARDEN , v. n. kaWinIBU, GanIBU, kaWorIBU, dfQIBU, karkaSIBU.

details.body: HARDSHIP: (1) kazwam, I got this h.: idaM kazwamupAgamam, K.s.;(2) kleSaH (= trouble: q.v.), do not [Page335] think of this h.: imaM parikle SaM hfdi mA kfTAH, Mah.; (3) duHKam (= pain), putting (you) into such h.: IdfSaM duHKamAnIya, Mah.; the h. s met in the (forest) Daṇḍaka: daRqakAyAM prAptAni duHKAni, R.

HARMONIOUS: I HARMONIC: q.v.II Sweet, melodious: q.v.: maDuraH (rA, raM).III Sym- -metrical: sarvaNgasaMvAdin (f. nI) (?).

HARMONIOUS , a. (Symphonious) ekatAlaH -lA -laM, ekasvaraH -rA -raM, saNgatasvaraH -rA -raM, samasvaraH -rA -raM, ekasvanaH -nA -naM, ekalayaH -yA -yaM, ekatAnaH -nA -naM. — (Melodious) susvaraH -rA -raM, maDurasvaraH -rA -raM, maDurasvanaH -nA -naM, sucArusvanaH -nA -naM, SrotrABirAmaH -mA -maM, SrotrasuKaH -KA -KaM, SrutisuKaH -KA -KaM, suKaSravaH -vA -vaM, suSrAvyaH -vyA -vyaM, suSabdaH -bdA -bdaM, maDuraH -rA -raM, maDukaH -kA -kaM. — (Consonant, agreeing) sadfSaH -SI -SaM, avirudDaH -dDA -dDaM, anuguRaH -RA -RaM, anusArI -riRI -ri (n), tulyaH -lyA -lyaM.
HARMONIOUSLY: I Of sounds:(1) raktam;(2) maDuram: v. Sweetly.II Symmetrically: expr. by adj.

HARMONIOUSLY , adv. (With symphony) svarEkyena, tAlEkyena, ekasvareRa, svarasaNgena, saNgatasvareRa. — (Melodiously) susvaraM, maDurasvareRa. — (Agreeably, in condordconcord) sadfSaM, avirudDaM, anusAreRa.
HARMONIOUSNESS , s. tAlEkyaM, svarEkyaM, svarasaNgaH, musvaratA, suSrAvyatA, mADuryyaM, sAdfSyaM, sadfSatA, avirudDatA.
HARMONIUM: a musical instrument *harmyonaH.
HARMONIZE: expr. by adj., the tones h.: SlizwAH svarAH; the arguments h.: saMvasanti tarkAH: v. To agree; h. the sound: nAdaM raktaM kuru (?).
To HARMONIZE , v. n. (Agree) sadfSIBU, sadfSaH -SI -Sam as, ekIBU, tulpIBU, anuguRIBU, na viruD (c. 7. -ruRadDi -rodDuM).
To HARMONIZE , v. a. sadfSIkf, sadfSaM -SIM -SaM kf, ekIkf, tulyIkf. — (Make musical) tAlEkyaM kf, svarEkyaM kf, susvarIkf, suSrAvyaM -vyAM -vyaM kf.

Harmony, s. tAlEkyaM, svarEkyaM, svarasaMgaH, eka-tAlaH-naH; ‘the triple h(armony)’ tOryatrikaM. 2 kalatA, suSrAvyatA, svaramADuryaM, susvaratA. 3 saMvAdaH, aviroDaH, EkyaM, ekatA, saMgaH, saM-yogaH, AnurUpyaM, sAdfSyaM; ‘h(armony) of thought or mind’ cittEkyaM, saMmati f., ekacittatA, matasaMvAdaH. 4 snehaBAvaH, prIti f., mEtryaM, snehaH. [Harmon]ic, [Harmon]ical, a. ekatAla-na, sama-eka-svara, susvara. [Harmon]ize, v. t. sadfSIkf 8 U. 2 svarEkyaM-tAlEkyaM-utpad c. v. i. sadfSIBU 1 P, ekI-tulyI-BU, saM-vad 1 P, na viruD pass. [Harmon]ous, a. ekatAla-na, eka-sama-svara, ekasvana, saMgatasvara-svana, ekalaya. 2 maDura-svara-svana, susvara, suKaSrava, SrotrABirAma, suSrAvya, SrutisuKa, kala, SravaRasuBagaM. 3 saMvAdin, sadfSa (SI f.), avirudDa, anuguRa, anurUpa. [Harmon]ously, adv. ekasvareRa-svanena. 2 maDurasvareRa-svanena, kalaM, maDuraM, susvaraM. 3 cittEkyena, aviroDena.

HARMONY: I Of sounds:(1) raktam, “raktaM nAma veRuvIRAdisvarARAmekIBAvaH”, Narada;(2) ekatAlaH (naH) (= unison: q.v.).II Melody, sweet- -ness: q.v.: mADuryam.III Agreement, sym- -metry: sarvANgasaMvaditA. (?).IV Peace, friend- -ship: Ekyam: v. A literary work: *EkyadarSanam.

HARMONY , s. (Of sound, musical concord) tAlEkyaM, svarEkyaM, svarasaNgaH, svarEkatA, ekatAlaH, ekatAnaH, ekalayaH; ‘of singing, dancing, and music,’ tOryyatrikaM, saNgItaM. — (Melody) susvaratA, suSrAvyatA, svaramADuryyaM, kalatA, tAlaH. — (Agreement, concord) EkyaM, ekatA, saNgaH, yogyatA, sAdfSyaM, aviroDaH, AnurUpyaM, anusAritA, saMyogaH, sanDiH m., dAkziRyaM; ‘of sentiment,’ sammati f., ekacittatA, cittEkyaM, maWEkyaM, parasparAnumatiH f., saMvAdaH. — (Friendship, love) prItiH f., mEtryaM, snehaH, sOhfdyaM.
Harness, v. t. sajjIkf 8 U, sannah 4 P or c., sajja a. kf. 2 (raTe) yuj 7 U, 10, ni-A-sam°. s. sajjA, sannAhaH, prasADanaM, paricCadaH, ABaraRaM. 2 aSvasajjA.
HARNESS (subs.): (aSva-) sajjA and sim. comp.s.
HARNESS (v.): I To equip.: sajjIkaroti.II To yoke: raTaM yunakti or yojayati (yfj, c. 7. and 10.), h. ed chariot: yukto raTaH, Ram. ii. 13. 23.
HARNESS , s. (Of a horse) aSvasajjA, aSvaparicCadaH, aSvABaraRaM, aSvapra- sADanaM, raTyasajjA. — (Accoutrements) sajjA, sannAhaH, paricCadaH, pariDAnaM, pAriRAhyaM, prasADanaM.

To HARNESS , v. a. (Fix a horse to a chariot) aSvaM raTe niyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM, c. 10. -yojayati -yituM) or yuj or Ayuj; raTam aSvena saMyuj. — (Put on the furniture of a horse) aSvaM sajjIkf or sasajjaM kf, aSvasajjanaM kf. — (Accoutre) sajj (c. 1. sajjati -jjituM), sannah (c. 4. -nahyati -nadDuM), pinah.
HARNESS-MAKER , s. aSvasajjAkarttA m. (rttf), aSvaparicCadakArI m. (n).
HARNESSED , p. p. raTaniyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, raTasaMyojitaH -tA -taM, AyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, saMsaktayugaH -gA -gaM, saMyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, sajjIkftaH -tA -taM, sajjitaH -tA -taM, sasajjaH -jjA -jjaM.
Harp, s. vallakI, vIRA, sAraMgI, vipaMcI. v. i. vIRAM vad c., ‘praise by h(arp)ing’ upa-vIRayati (D.); ‘h(arp) on’ punaruktyA-pOnaH-punyena-vad 1 P, prapaMcayati (D.). [Harp]er, s. vIRAvAdakaH.
HARP (subs.): *triBujavIRAH v. Lute.
HARP (v.): I Lit.: vAdayati (c. of vad): v. To play.II Fig.: to dwell tediously on the same theme: BUyoBUyo gAyati (gE, c. 1.) (?).
HARP , s. vallakI, vIRA, vipaYcI -YcikA, tantrI, rudrI.

To HARP , v. n. (Play on the harp) vallakIM or vIRAM vad (c. 10. vAdayati -yituM); ‘celebrate on the harp,’ upavIRa (nom. upavIRayati -yituM); ‘harp on a subject,’ atiprasaNgaM kf, punaruktiM kf, prapaYcaM kf, dIrGasUtraH -trA -traM BU.
HARPER, HARPIST: triBujavIRAvAdakaH.
HARPER , s. vIRAvAdaH -dakaH, vERikaH, vIRApARiH, vallakIvAdaH.
Harpoon, s. timiveDanI. [Harpoon]er, s. timi-veDakaH.
HARPOON: I Subs.: perh. SUlam.II Verb: SUlona gfhvAti (grah, c. 9.).
HARPOON , s. timiveDanArTaM SUlaH, DIvarI, timiveDanI, makaraveDanI.
HARPOONEER, HARPOONER: SUlaveDakaH (?).
HARPOONER , s. timiveDakaH, makaraveDakaH, mInarAGAtI m. (n).
HARPSICHORD , s. tAntravAdyaviSezaH, tantrI, vallakI, vipaYcikA.
Harpy, s. rAkzasI.
HARPY: I A fabulous monster: kzuDA (??). II An extortioner, plunderer: q.v.: nizkarzakaH.
HARPY , s. kavikalpitaH strImuKo gfDrapakziSarIraH sulubDaSIlo jantuBedaH. — (Plunderer) apahArakaH, sAhasikaH, vipralumpakaH, upadravI m. (n).
Harridan, s. vfdDaveSyA, jaratI gaRikA.
HARRIDAN: (1) vfdDaveSayA;(2) vfdDakuwwinI, K. s. xii. 79.: v. Prostitute, old.
HARRIDAN , s. vfdDabanDakI, jIrRaveSyA, vfdDA gaRikA.
HARRIER: SaSaSvan (m.): v. Hound.
HARRIER , s. SaSakAKewakaH kukkuraBedaH, SaSakAKewe Sikzito mfgavyaSvA m. (n).

Harrow, v. t. atyaMtaM pIq 10 or tud 6 P, saMtap c., prabAD 1 A; See Grieve. 2 lo-zwAni Bid 7 P or vidF 10. s. kowi(wI)-SaH, lozwaBedanaH. [Harrow]ing, a. hfdaya-marma-cCid, aruMtud, hfdispfS, atiduHKAvaha.
HARROW (subs.): (1) kowi(wI)SaH;(2) jityaH (rare);(3) lozwaBedanaH, A.
HARROW (v.): I Lit.: kowiSaM cAlayati (c. of cal) (with loc.)II To rend, grind: pinazwi, nis- (piz, c. 7.).
HARROW , s. kowiSaH, kowISaH, lozwaBedanaH, lozwaGnaH, AkarzaRI, jityaH.

To HARROW , v. a. kowiSena BUmiM kfz (c. 6. kfzati, krazwuM), pUrvvoktayantreRa mfllozwAni Bid (c. 7. Binatti, BettuM) or dF in caus. (dArayati -yituM). — (Lacerate, torment) vidF in caus. santap (c. 10. -tApayati -yituM), kfz (c. 10. karzayati -yituM).
HARROWER: I Properly: kowiSacAlakaHII =harrier: q.v.:
HARROWER , s. kowiSena BUmikarzakaH or mfllozwaBedakaH.
HARROWING (adj.): aruntudaH (dA, daM): v. Heart- -rending, horrible.
HARROWING , a. vidArakaH -kA -kaM, aruntudaH -dA -daM, santApakaH -kA -kaM.
To HARRY , v. a. bAD (c. 1. bADate -DituM), pIq (c. 10. pIqayati -yituM), kliS (c. 9. kliSnAti, kleSituM), vyaT (c. 10. vyaTayati -yituM).

Harsh, a. karkaSa, paruza, rUkza, nizWura, kaWora, ugra, kaWina, krUra, kawu; ‘h(arsh) to the touch’ amasfRa, duHKasparSa, rUkza; ‘h(arsh) to the taste’ Sukta, kazAya; ‘h(arsh) to the ear’ visvara, karRakawu, duHSrAvya, paruza, karkaSa. [Harsh]ly, adv. nizWuraM, paruzaM, rUkzaM; krOryeRa, ugraM. [Harsh]ness, s. pAruzyaM, kArkaSyaM, rUkzatA, kAWinyaM.

HARSH: (1) karkaSaH (SA, SaM), h. like the lotus stalk: aBBojanAlakarkaSaH, Vi.; this man is h. (in appearance): karkaSo'yaM puruzaH, D. iv.; h. to the ear: karRakarkaSaH (SA, SaM), N.; this is the h. end of my peacefulness: eza Be praSamasya karkaSaH pariRAmaH, Vi. ii.;(2) rUkzaH (kzA, kzaM) (= rough), lotus-film is sweet (but) h. (in taste): BfRAlaM maDuraM rUkzaB, Bha; in a h. tone: rUkzeRa svareRa, Mah.; of exceedingly h. resolution towards the daughter of Janaka: janakAtmajAyAM nitAntarUkzAminiveSaH (SA, SaM) R. xiv. 43;(3) paruzaH (zA, zaM) (of words), h. language: paruzaM vAkyam, Ram.: v. Also hard, cruel.

HARSH , a. (Rough to the touch) rUkzaH -kzA -kzaM, rukzaH -kzA -kzaM, paruzaH -zA -zaM, duHKasparSaH -rSA -rSaM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, vizamaH -mA -maM, amasfRaH -RA -RaM. — (Rough to the ear) karRakawuH -wuH -wu, karkaSasvanaH -nA -naM, karkaSasvaraH -rA -raM, visvaraH -rA -raM, kuSrAvyaH -vyA -vyaM, viJarJaraH -rA -raM. — (Rough to the taste, sour) SuktaH -ktA -ktaM, amlarasaH -sA -saM, kazAyaH -yA -yaM, kazAyAnvitaH -tA -taM. — (Austere, severe, crabbed) nizWuraH -rA -raM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, ugraH -grA -graM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, krUraH -rA -raM, kawuH -wuH -wu, kaWoraH -rA -raM, jaraWaH -WA -WaM, kIwakaH -kA -kaM, jAlmaH -lmA -lmaM; ‘harsh words,’ karkaSavAkyaM, paruzavacanaM, paruzoktiH f., SuktaM, vikruzwavacanaM.
HARSHLY: (1) karkaSam;(2) rUkzam;(3) paruzam, Mah. or paruzAkzaram, R. (in harsh words): v. Also cruelly.

HARSHLY , adv. (Roughly) rUkzaM, paruzaM, karkaSaM, vizamaM. — (Discor- dantly) visvaraM, karkaSaM, karkaSasvareRa, viJarJaraM. — (Severely, austerely) nizWuraM, nEzWuryyeRa, karkaSaM, kArkaSyena, sakArkaSyaM, kaWinaM, kAwinyena, ugraM, kaWoraM, kawu.

HARSHNESS: (1) karkaSatA, -tvam or kArkaSyam, R.;(2) rUkztA or rOkzyam, forgive my h.: rOkzyaM me kzamasva, R. xiv. 56.;(3) paruzatA or pAruzyam (of language), h. is not good: paruzatA na sADvI, Ki. ix. 39.

HARSHNESS , s. (Roughness to the touch) rUkzatA, rOkzyaM, paruzatA, pAruzyaM, kArkaSyaM, vEzamyaM, duHKasparSatvaM. — (Roughness to the ear) karRakawutA, karkaSatA, visvaratA, kuSrAvyatA. — (Roughness to the taste) SuktatA, amlatA, kazAyatvaM, kawutA. — (Severity, austerity) nizWuratA, nEzWuryyaM, karkaSatA, kArkaSyaM, ugratA, kaWinatA, kAWinyaM, krUratA, kaWoratA, kawutA, pArupyaM, SuktatA, vyalIkatA, jAlmatA.
Harslet, s. SUkarAMtrARi (pl.).
HARSLET , HASLET, s. SUkarAntrARi n. pl., SUkarasya hfdyakfdantrAdi.
Hart, s. mfgaH, hariRaH, eRaH, kuraMgaH-gamaH.
HART: (1) mfgaH;(2) hariRaH;(3) kuraNgaH, -maH.
HART , s. mfgaH, hariRaH, kuraNgaH -NgakaH -NgamaH, kfzRasAraH, eRaH.
HARTSHORN , s. mfgaSfNgaM, mfgavizARaH; ‘spirits of hartshorn,’ mfgaSf- NgAdiniryAsaH, mfgaSfNgAdinizkarzito rasaH.
Harum-scarum, a. pramAdin, asAvaDAna, sAhasin.

Harvest, s. lavaH, SasyasaMgrahakAlaH, Sasyalavana-saMcaya-samayaH. 2 SasyAni, saMgfhIta-lUna-SasyaM. v. t. SasyaM lU 9 U or saMgrah 9 P or saMci 5 U; ‘h(arvest)-lord’ praDAnaH SasyasaMgrAhakaH; ‘h(arvest)-man’ SasyasaMgrAhakaH-Cettf m.
HARVEST (subs.): I The season: lavaH, h. is the reaping time: lavaH SasyacCedanakAlaH, Nil.II The crops: SasyAni (n. pl.).
HARVEST (v.): lunAti (lU, c. 9.), in sowing, in h. ing: vapane lavane, Pa: v. To reap.

HARVEST , s. (The season of gathering the corn) SasyasaNgrahakAlaH, SasyaCedanakAlaH, SasyakarttanasamayaH, SasyalavanakAlaH, goDUmakarttanakAlaH, SasyasaYcayakAlaH, SasyasaNgrahaH. — (Gathered corn) saNgfhItaSasyaM, lUnaSasyaM, CinnaSasyaM.
To HARVEST , v. a. SasyasaNgrahaM kf, SasyaM saNgrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM) or Cid (c. 7. Cinatti, CettuM) or lU (c. 9. lunAti, lavituM) or ci (c. 5. cinoti, cetuM), SasyasaYcayaM kf.
HARVEST-HOME: navAnnam (?).
HARVEST-HOME , s. SasyasaNgrahakAlamuddiSya grAmyajanasevito mahotsavaH.
HARVEST-LORD , s. SasyaCettFRAM maDyAt praDAnaCettA m. (ttf), SrezWaH Sasyasa- NgrAhakaH or SasyasaNgrahItA m. (tf), praDAnalavakaH.
HARVEST-MAN , HARVESTER, s. SasyaCettA m. (ttf), SasyasaNgrAhakaH, SasyasaNgrahItA m. (tf), SasyasaYcayI m. (n), SasyalavakaH, DAnyAdisa- YcayakArI m. (n).
HARVESTER: (1) lAvakaH, N. d.;(2) lavanakartf (f. trI), K. b.: v. Reaper.
HASH (subs.): kuwwitaM sidDamAMsam (?); vesavAraH, Sr.
HASH (v.): kuwwayati (kuww, c. 10.): v. To chop, mince.
To HASH , v. a. KaRqaM KaRqaM kf, KaRqaSaH kf or Cid (c. 7. Cinatti, CettuM) or viCid, SakalIkf, KaRqIkf.
HASH , s. (Hashed meat) vyaYjanAdinA saha sidDaM CinnamAMsaM or KaRqamAMsaM.
HASP: kuqupaH (?).
HASP , s. kuqupaH, sanDiH m., banDanI, banDanakuqupaH.
To HASP , v. a. pUrvvoktakuqupena banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM).

sanskrit.slp1: BajanaSAlAyAM pIWaviSezo yasminn ISvarapUjako jAnadvayaM nyasya
sanskrit.word: भजनशालायां पीठविशेषो यस्मिन्न् ईश्वरपूजको जानद्वयं न्यस्य
sanskrit.iast: bhajanaśālāyāṃ pīṭhaviśeṣo yasminn īśvarapūjako jānadvayaṃ nyasya

details.body: HASSOCK: (1) kawaH;(2) kuSAsanam (used by Brahmins).
HASSOCK , s. BajanaSAlAyAM pIWaviSezo yasminn ISvarapUjako jAnadvayaM nyasya pUjAM karoti, pAdapaH, vistaraH.

Haste, s. tvarA, vegaH, javaH, tUrRi f., saMBramaH, SIGratA, kzipratA, taras n., raBasaH-saM, tvarita-ASu-gati f., gamanaM. [Hast]en, v. i. ‘make h(asten)’ tvar 1 A, satvaraM-ASu-gam or cal or DAv 1 P; ‘h(asten) towards’ aBidru 1 P. v. t. tvar c. (tvarayati). Hasty, a. satvara, tvarita, kzipra, tUrRa, SIGra, tvarAvat, druta, avilaMbin, ASukArin. 2 sAhasin, avimfSya-asamIkzya-kArin or -kft. 3 SIGra-kopin, sulaBakopa. Hastily, adv. SIGraM, kzipraM, satvaraM, avilaMbaM, tvaritaM, ASu, Jawiti, drutaM. 2 sahasA, saraBasaM, sasaMBramaM, vegena. 3 kopena, saMraMBeRa.
HASTE (subs.): tvarA, of doubled speed from h.: tvarAdviguRaraMhas (mfn.), Ku. ii. 68.; to make h.: v. To haste; in h.: v. Hastily.

HASTE, HASTEN (v.): I Intrans: tvarate (tvar, c. 1.), h., h. the sages are calling: tvarasva, tvarasva fzayaH SabdAyante, Sa.: v. Also to fly, run. II Trans:(1) tvarayati (c. of tvar), who h. s crowds in the way: vfndAni tvarayati paTi, Me.; h. his dinner: tvarayAsya Bojanam, v. ii.

HASTE , s. tvarA, tUrRiH f., tvaraRaM, tvaritaM, satvaratA, samBramaH, SIGratA, SEGryaM, kzipratA, drutatvaM, vegaH -gitA, AvegaH, javaH, prajavaH, jUtiH f., jUrRiH f., taras n., raBasaH, avilambaH, ASukAritvaM, kziprakAritvaM, tvarita- gatiH f., ASugamanaM, raMhatiH f.; ‘in haste,’ sasamBramaM, satvaraM; ‘to make haste,’ tvar (c. 1. tvarate -rituM); ‘make haste,’ tvaryyatAM.
To HASTE , HASTEN, v. a. tvar in caus. (tvarayati -yituM), santvar, kzepa (nom. kzepayati -yituM), kziprIkf, drutataraM -rAM -raM kf.

To HASTE , HASTEN, v. n. tvar (c. 1. tvarate -rituM), santvar, atitvar, SIGra (nom. SIGrAyate), taraRa (nom. taraRyati); ‘to move with haste,’ ASu or satvaraM or tvaritaM gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM) or cal (c. 1. calati -lituM), dru (c. 1. dravati, drotuM), DAv (c. 1. DAvati -vituM); ‘to hasten towards,’ aBidru, Adru, samAdru, samupadru, pratidru, aBiDAv.
HASTILY: (1) tvaritam;(2) satvaram;(3) tvarAnvitaH (tA, taM) and sim. comp.s, Ram. ii. 13. 20.; (4) kzipram: v. Quickly. Ph.: should not do a thing h.: sahasA vidaDIta na kriyAm, Ki. ii. 30.
HASTILY , adv. satvaraM, tvaritaM, kzipraM, SIGraM, ASu, tUrRaM, sasamBramaM, saraBasaM, sahasA, drutaM, vegatas, avilambitaM, sapadi, Jawiti. — (Passionately) kroDAt, kopAt, kroDAvizwatvAt.
HASTINAPUR , s. (The city) hastinApuraM, hastinIpuraM, gajAhvaM -hvayaM.
HASTINESS: I Haste: tvarA.II Rashness: q.v.: asamIkzya- or AvimfzyakAritA.III Irrita- -bility: SIGrAgitA, and sim. comp.s.
HASTINESS , s. (Haste, speed) satvaratA -tvaM, SIGratA, SEGryaM, kzipratA, drutatA, ASutA. — (Precipitation) kziprakAritA, ASukAritvaM, sAhasaM. — (Of temper) SIGakopitvaM.
HASTINGS , s. pl. praTamasatIlakaH, prAkpUrRakAlAt KAdanIyaH sAtilakaH.
HASTY: I Quick: q.v.: tvaritaH (tA, taM).II Rash: q.v.: asamIkzya- or avimfzya-kArin (f. RI), III Of words: avimfzya (f. zyA) or anyAya-, in comp. (= unjust).

HASTY , a. (Quick, expeditious) tvaritaH -tA -taM, tvarAvAn -vatI -vat (t), tvarAyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, satvaraH -rA -raM, tvarAnvitaH -tA -taM, tUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, SIGraH -GrA -GraM, kzipraH -prA -praM, drutaH -tA -taM, SIGrakArI -riRI -ri (n), kziprakArI &c., ASukArI &c., avilambaH -mbA -mbaM -mbI -mbinI -mbi (n), avilambitaH -tA -taM. — (Rash) sAhasI -sinI -si (n). — (In temper) SIGrakopI -pinI -pi (n), sulaBakopaH -pA -paM.

HEAD (subs.): I Lit.:(1) Siras (n.), the h. aches: Siro rujati, Sr.; with a shake of the h.: saSiraHkampam, Ve.;(2) mUrdDan (m.), three-h. ed: trimUrdDan (mfn.), Vi.;(3) mastakam, I will hash your h.: mastakaM te kuwwayizyAmi, Mr.;(4) SIrzam, with the frightful h. s. cut off: CinnEH SIrzErBayaNkarEH, A. r.; (5) muRqam (in contempt), shaving the h.: muRqaM muRqayitvA, Mu.;(6) tuRqam (rare), the h. is grey: palitaM tuRqam, J.II Chief, leader: q.v.: agraRI. Ph.: the h. of the atheists: nAstikaSiromaRiH, Da. III Of things: agram. Ph.: at the h. of a battle: raRaSirasi, raRamUrdDani, etc.; h. of a mount: girimUrdDA; h. of a wound: vraRamuKam, Ki.IV Source: q.v.V A topic of discourse: vizayaH.VI Intellect: q.v.:VII An indi- -vidual: q.v.:VIII Force, strength: q.v. Ph.: to come to a h. (of wounds): pAkaM vrajati; h. or tail: eza pArSvo'nyo vA (?).; neither h. nor tail: na kiYcidapi; to one's h.: samakzam; to make h.: v. To advance.

Health, s. kuSalaM, arogaH, susTatA, vArttaM, rogABAvaH, nirAmayatvaM, susTiti f., ArogyaM, svAsTyaM, anAmayaM, kalyatvaM-tA, SarIrasuKaM, arogitA. 2 prakfti f., SarIrAvasTA, SarIra-sTitiH-prakftiH; ‘of a delicate h(ealth)’ prakfti-komala-durbala; ‘he is in good h(ealth)’ susTosO, kuSalamasya. [Health]ful, [Health]y, a. Arogyavat, arogin, nIroga, nIrujaj, svasTa, vyADi-rahita, nirAmaya, vArtta, susTa, kalya, kuSalin, nirvyADi; ‘became as h(ealthy) as before’ pUrvavat prakftisTaH samajAyata. 2 Arogya-suKa-kara (rI f.), paTya, hita, svAsTyajanaka, suKAvaha. [Health]fulness, See (s.).

HEALTH: (1) Arogyam (best equiv.) (also arogitA or arogatA), strength, h.: SaktirAgogyam, Ph.: to recover h.: ArogyaM prApnoti; to wish h.: ArogyamicCati, Kat.;(2) svAsTyam, to keep h.: svAsTyaM rakzati, Sr.;(3) anAmayam (rare), says this, wishing you h.: anAmayapraSnapUrvakamidamAha, Sa. v. To be in good, bad h.: susTaH (sTA, sTaM), a-: v. Well, ill.

HEALTH , s. svAsTyaM, svasTatA, arogaH, ArogyaM, arogitA, susTatA, susTitiH f., anAmayaM, nirAmayatA, rogABAvaH, kalyatvaM -tA, kuSalaM, SarIrakuSalaM, SarIrasuKaM, vArttaH, utpAlI. — (Bad health) asvAsTyaM, asusTatA, SarIraduHsTitiH f., rogitA, sarogatA; ‘health to you,’ svasti, kuSalaM te.
HEALTH-GIVING: svAsTyakaraH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s.
HEALTH-OFFICER: svAsTyADikftaH (?) and sim. comp.s.
HEALTHFUL , a. arogI -giRI -gi (n), nIrogaH -gA -gaM, ArogyaH -gyI -gyaM, susTaH -sTA -sTaM, svasTaH -sTA -sTaM, nirAmayaH -yA -yaM. See HEALTHY.
HEALTHFULLY , adv. arogeRa, sArogyaM, nirAmayaM, svAsTyena, kuSalaM.
HEALTHFULNESS , s. arogitA -tvaM, svAsTyaM, nirAmayatA, kalyatvaM.
HEALTHILY, HEALTHFULLY: (1) susTam;(2) nirA- mayam; etc.
HEALTHILY , adv. sArogyaM, sAnAmayaM, SarIrasvAsTyena, svasTavat.
HEALTHINESS: I Of men:(1) svAsTyam;(2) arogitA and sim. comp.s.II Of places: expr. by adj.
HEALTHINESS , s. svAsTyaM, svasTatA, ArogyaM, arogitA, susTatA, SarIra- susTitiH f., nirAmayatvaM, anAmayatvaM, kalyatvaM -tA -rogABAvaH.
HEALTHLESS , a. asvasTaH -sTA -sTaM, asusTaSarIraH -rA -raM, sarogaH -gA -gaM.
HEALTHSOME , a. svAsTyajanakaH -kA -kaM, roganivarttakaH -kA -kaM, rogaGnaH -GnI -GnaM.

HEALTHY: I Of men:(1) susTaH (sTA, sTaM); (2) arogaH (gA, gaM), nirAmayaH (yA, yaM) and sim. comp.s. (= without disease);(3) kuSalin (f. nI) (= well: q.v.).II Of places:(1) kzemya (f. myA), M. vii. 212.;(2) anAmayakzamaH (mA, maM), K. b. and sim. comp.s.III Of food:(1) hitaH (tA, taM) (= good: q.v.):(2) paTya (f. TyA), Sr.: v. Wholesome.

HEALTHY , a. susTaH -sTA -sTaM, susTitaH -tA -taM, arogI -giRI -gi (n), nIrogaH -gA -gaM, nIrujaH -jA -jaM, nIruk m. f. n. (j), nirAmayaH -yA -yaM, svasTaH -sTA -sTaM, sahArogyaH -gyA -gyaM, kalpaH -lyA -lyaM, kuSalI -linI -li (n), nirvyADiH -DiH -Di, vyADihInaH -nA -naM, rogahInaH -nA -naM, caNgaH -NgA -NgaM, vArttaH -rttA -rttaM, nizpIqaH -qA -qaM. — (Causing health) svAsTyajanakaH -kA -kaM, ArogyakaraH -rI -raM, anAmayakaraH -rI -raM.

HEAP (subs.): (1) rASiH, h. s. of jewels: ratnarASIn, Si.;(2) cayaH, ni-, saM-, h. of ashes: BasmanAM cayaH, Ki.;(3) puYjaH;(4) pUgaH;(5) stomaH: v. Also pile.
HEAP (v.): I Lit.:(1) rASIkaroti, pUgIkaroti, etc.;(2) cinoti, saM-, ni-, A-, pra-, samA-, (ci, c. 5.): v. Also to collect.II Of favours etc.: varzati (vfz, c. 1.): v. To shower.

HEAP , s. rASiH m. -SI f., saYcayaH, nicayaH, cayaH, citiH f., pracayaH, piRqaH, prakaraH, utkaraH, nikaraH, oGaH, puYjaH, pUgaH, stUpaH, stomaH, vfndaM, samUhaH, samavAyaH, sannayaH, samudAyaH, cAyaH, saMsTAnaM, saNgrahaH, kUwaH; ‘a heap of grass,’ tfRarASiH m., tfRavistaraH, tfRyA.

To HEAP , v. a. rASIkf, Aci (c. 5. -cinoti -cetuM), samAci, saYci, samAkzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM), piRqIkf, piRq (c. 1. piRqate, c. 10. piRqayati -yituM), oGIkf, vfndIkf, ekatrIkf, ekatra kf, puYjIkf, pUgIkf.

HEAPED , p. p. rASIkftaH -tA -taM, rASIBUtaH -tA -taM, AcitaH -tA -taM, upacitaH -tA -taM, samupacitaH -tA -taM, saYcitaH -tA -taM, piRqitaH -tA -taM, piRqIkftaH -tA -taM, piRqIBUtaH -tA -taM, ekOGaBUtaH -tA -taM, puYjitaH -tA -taM, pUgIkftaH -tA -taM, saNkalitaH -tA -taM, saNgUQaH -QA -QaM, puYjizWaH -zWA -zWaM, ekapiRqIBUtaH -tA -taM, ekatrIBUtaH -tA -taM, samUQaH -QA -QaM, paryyastaH -stA -staM; ‘heaped with flowers,’ kusumacitaH -tA -taM.

HEAPTH , s. agnikuRqaM, vitAnaM, culliH f. -llI, aSmantaM, antikA, upacAyyaH, pakzaH.
HEAPY , a. piRqI -RqinI -Rqi (n), nicayI -yinI -yi (n), utkarIyaH -yA -yaM.

Hear, v. t. Sru 5 P, samA-A-kaR 10, niSam 4 P or c. (SAmayati); ‘h(ear) cases’ vyavahArAn dfS 1 P, kAryARi avekz 1 A or vicar c. or anusaM-DA 3 U. v. i. vArtAM Sru; ‘I have not heard from him for a long time’ ciraM tadvArtA mayA na SrutA. [Hear]er, s. Srotf m., SrAvakaH, AkarRayitf m. [Hear]ing, s. SravaRaM, Sruti f., AkarRanaM, niSA-manaM. 2 (In law) darSanaM, avekzaRaM, anusaM-DAnaM; ‘the organ of h(earing)’ SravaReMdriyaM, SrotraM; ‘within h(earing)’ SravaRagocare, SrutipaTa-vartin. Hearsay, s. janaSruti f., karRa-paraMparA, janavAdaH-pravAdaH, kiMvadaMtI; ‘know it by h(earsay)’ iti karRaparaMparayA SrutaM.

HEAR: I Lit.:(1) SfRotti (Sru, c. 5.), he h. s. without ears: SfRotyakarRaH, S.; we h. he will go to hermitage: tapovanaM gamizyatIti SrUyate, Mu. iv.; I will h. their confidential talk: SfRomi viSvasta- kaTitAnyAsAm, Sa. iii.;(2) AkarRayati, sam-, (karRa, c. 10.) (= perceive by the ear), h. ing the noise of geese: haMsanAdAnAkarRayan, B. ii. 7;(3) niSAmayati (Sam, c. 10.) (rare), h. ing of the succes of enemies: niSamya sidDiM dvizatAm, Ki. i. 27. II To listen to: SfRoti, [princes] h. him who flatters day and night: tasya vacanaM SfRvanti yo'harniSaM stOti, K.; a king after rising is to h. about all receipts and disbursements: utTitena rAjYA kftsnamAyavyayajAtaM Srotavyam, D. viii.III In law: paSyati (dfS, c. 1.) (= to see), he personally h. d complaints: sa svayaM vyavahArAn dadarSa, R. xvii. 39. IV To receive letters: I have not h. d from him for a long time: *bahoH kAlAt tasya patrARi na mayADigatAni; distressed at not h. ing (of him) for good many days: bahudivasApagame ca vArtayA vinottAmyantI, K. ii.: v. Also to learn.

To HEAR , v. a. and n. Sru (c. 5. SfRoti, SrotuM), upaSru, samupaSru, anuSru, pariSru, AkarR (c. 10. -karRayati -yituM), niSam (c. 10. -SAmayati -yituM, c. 4. -SAmyati -SamituM), viniSam, sanniSam, SravaRendriyeRa or karRadvAreRa upalaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM) or buD (c. 1. boDati -DituM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM), SravaRaM kf; ‘having heard,’ SrutvA, niSAmya.
HEARD , p. p. SrutaH -tA -taM, AkarRitaH -tA -taM; ‘as heard,’ yaTASrutaM.

HEARER (1) Srotf (f. trI), you will get a h.: lapsyase SrotAram, Mu. l.;(2) SrAvaka (f. vikA), all those h. s: sarvAneva tAn SrAvakAn, K.;(3) SfRvat (f. tI) (= actually hearing), to draw the hearts of the h. s: SfRvatAM mano hartum.
HEARER , s. SrotA m. (tf), SravaRakarttA m. (rttf), AkarRayitA m. (tf).

HEARING (subs.): I The act: SravaRam, from first h.: praTamaSravARAt, M. n.: v. To hear.II The faculty;(1) SravaRaSaktiH;(2) SrutiH.III An audience: q.v.: darSanam.IV Judicial: darSanam, of not h. or of h. improperly: adarSanAnyaTAdarSanayoH, Mit.V Reach of the ear.: SravaRavizayaH. Ph.: within h.: SravaRagocaraH (rA, raM); out of h.: asaMSravaH (vA, vaM); going beyond the h. of a cow's lowing: gorutAntaramatikramya, D.v.

HEARING , s. SravaRaM, SrutiH f., AkarRanaM, niSamanaM, niSAmanaM; ‘sense of hearing,’ SrotraM, SravaRendriyaM; ‘out of hearing,’ asaMSravaH -vA -vaM, karRAgocaraH -rA -ra; ‘out of the hearing of the master,’ guror asaMSrave; ‘within hearing,’ karRagocaraH -rA -raM, karRaSravaH -vA -vaM.
HEARKEN: AkarRayati (karR, c. 10.): v. Listen, hear.
To HEARKEN , v. n. Sru (c. 5. SfRoti, SrotuM), AkarR (c. 10. -karRayati -yituM), niSam (c. 10. -SAmayati -yituM), SravaRaM kf.
HEARKENER , s. SrotA m. (tf), SravaRakArI m. (n), niSamanakArI m.
HEARSAY: janaSrutiH: v. Rumour, Ph.: h. evi- dence: SrutasAkzyam (?), Mit.
HEARSAY , s. kiMvadantI, janaSrutiH f., janavAdaH, janaravaH.
Hearse, s. preta-Sava-yAnaM-vAhanaM.
HEARSE: (1) SavayAnam;(2) pretaSakawam, Say.
HEARSE , s. SavavAhanaM, SavayAnaM, pretavahanArTaM KawvA, pretavahanasADanaM, kawaH.

Heart, s. hfdayaM, hfd n. 2 (The substance) bukkA, agramAMsaM, bukkAgramAMsaM. 3 (Mind) cittaM, manas n., cetas n., mAnasaM, hfdayaM, aMtaHkaraRaM, Atman m., aMtarAtman m., svAMtaM. 4 uras n., vakzas n., vakzaHsTalaM. 5 marman n. 6 snehaH, praRayaH, rAgaH, BAvaH. 7 udaraM, garBaH, aByaMtaraM, aMtar in comp. 8 sattvaM, DEryaM, pOruzaM, tejas n.; ‘take h(eart)’ A-samA-Svas 2 P; DEryaM avalaMb 1 A, avazwaMB 9 P; ‘learn or get by h(eart)’ kaMWasTa a. kf 8 U, aByas 4 P; ‘keep in the h(eart)’ cittekf, avaDf 10; ‘out of h(eart)’ dIna-Kinna-citta; ‘at h(eart)’ aMtaH; ‘with all oneʼs h(eart)’ ‘h(eart) and soul’ prakAmaM, kAmaM, sotsAhaM, sarvAtmanA; ‘he has applied himself to the work h(eart) and soul’ sarvAtmanA tasmi nkarmaRi sa vyApftaH; ‘to oneʼs h(eart)ʼs content’ yaTecCaM, paryAptaM, AcittatozaM, kAmaM, prakAmaM, nikAmaM, izwaM, yaTepsitaM; ‘from the h(eart)’ nirvyAjaM, sotsAhaM, nirvya-lIkaM; ‘h(eart)-ache’ hfdayasaMtApaH, manovyADiH, hfdayavyaTA-pIqA-vedanA, manastApaH, mAnasI vyaTA; ‘h(eart)-broken’ Bagna-mAnasa, aMtarBinna, Binnahfdaya; ‘h(eart)-burn’; hfdayavedanA, manastApaH; hfllAsaH, amlapittaM; ‘h(eart)-ease’ hfdayasvAsTyaM-suKaM, cittaSAMti, nirvfti f.; ‘h(eart)-felt’ avyAja, nirvyAja, vAstavika (kI f.), akftrima; ‘h(eart)-breaking, -rending, -wounding’ marma-Bid-spfS-cCid, hfdaya-marma-Bedin-cCedin, hfdispfS, aruMtuda, cittodvegajanaka; ‘h(eart)-robbing’ manohara, cittahArin; ‘h(eart)-sick’ durmanas, udvignacitta, Kinna-vizaRRa-hfdaya; See Dejected; ‘h(eart)-struck, -wounded’ vidDamarman, kzata-vidDa-hfdaya; ‘h(eart)-whole’ akzata-aBinna-hfdaya. [Heart]less, a. nirvIrya, ni-stejas; BIruhfdaya, nissattva, nizpOruza, klIba. 2 nirdaya, krUra, kaWorahfdaya, nirGfRa. [Heart]lessly, adv. nirvIryaM, klIbavat. 2 nirdayaM, krUratayA. [Heart]lessness, s. apOruzaM, klIbatA, nirvIryatvaM. 2 nirdayatvaM, kaWoratA. Hearty, a. sarala, nirvyalIka, nizkapawa, nirvyAja, SudDAM-taHkaraRa; See Frank. 2 akftrima, akftaka, sotsAha, utsuka, sollAsa, sasneha, hfdya; hfdayaMgama, snehanirBara; ‘a h(earty) friend’ hfdayaMgamaH saKA. 3 vIryavat, sapOruza; kalya, susTa. [Hearti]ly, adv. nirvyalIka, nizkapawaM, nirvyAjaM. 2 sollAsaM, sotsAhaM, prakAmaM, sarvAtmanA, saMtuzwa-cetasA, kAmataH, sAnaMdaM, sAhlAdaM, cittasaMtozeRa. 3 savIryaM. [Hearty]ness, s. sAralyaM, akftrimatA, avyAjatvaM; utsAhaH, OtsukyaM, vIryaM, tejas n., pOruzaM.

HEART: I Lit.: hfdayam or hfd (n.), has any body two h. s: kiM kasyacidDfdayadvayaM Bavati,. P. iv. 1.II Fig.:(1) hfdayam, touching the h.: hfdayagrAhin (f. RI), Ki.;(2) cetaH, the unsteady h. runs behind: DAvati [Page340] paScAdasaMsTitaM cetaH, Sa.;(3) manas. (n.), even at h.: manasApi, R.: v. Mind.III The interior of anything: udaram, the h. of the city: purodaram, B. xiv. 10.IV Courage, spirit: q.v.: sattvaB, Ph.: take h.: praPullamanA Bava.V Real intention: aBiprAyaH, Ph.: to get by h.: kaRWasTaM (f. sTAM) karoti; to have in h.: hfdaye karoti; he has set his whole h. on it: sa sarvAtmanEvAsminnimagnaH; he took it to h.: *idaM tasya hfdayaM pasparSa or mano KedayAmAsa; I “find in the h.” that he is a friend: *sa mitramiti hfdayaM mAM kaTayati.

HEART , s. (The seat of life in an animal) hfdayaM, hfd n., hftpiRqaM, raktASayaH, agramAMsaM, bukkAgramAMsaM, marmma n. (n), bukkaH -kkA -kkaM, bfkkaH, kantuH m., rikaM, Bazat m. — (Seat of feeling) cittaM, cetas, hfdayaM, antaHkaraRaM, antaHprakftiH f., antarAtmA m. (n), AtmA m., manas n., antarBAvaH, mAnasaM, svAntaM. — (The breast) vakzas n., vakzassTalaM, vakzaHsTalaM. — (Vital part) marmma n. (n), marmmasTAnaM -sTalaM, hfdayasTAnaM -sTalaM. — (Inner part of any thing) garBaH, udaraM, aByantaraM or expressed by antar prefixed; as, ‘the heart of the city,’ antarnagaraM. — (Courage, spirit) vIryyaM, SOryyaM, tejas, sattvaM, pOruzaM. — (Affection) snehaH, praRayaH, hArddaM, BAvaH, rAgaH; ‘my heart beats,’ spandate or kampate hfdayaM me; ‘it goes to my heart,’ marmma Binatti or spfSati; ‘to take heart,’ ASvas (c. 2. -Svasiti -tuM), samASvas; [Page337-b+ 51] ‘to learn by heart,’ aByas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM), rUpaM kf; ‘learnt by heart,’ kaRWasTaH -sTA -sTaM, aByastaH -stA -staM; ‘learn- ing by heart,’ rUpaM; ‘to be out of heart,’ dInamanaskaH -skA -skaM BU; ‘pure in heart,’ nirmmalAntaHkaraRaH -RA -RaM; ‘with all one's heart,’ kAmaM, prakAmaM; ‘heart's desire,’ manovAYCitaM; ‘from the heart,’ antaHkaraRena; ‘heart-searching,’ cittajYaH -jYA -jYaM.

HEART-BROKEN: (1) magnahfdayaH (yA, yaM);(2) BagnamAnasaH (sA, saM), Mah.; and sim. comp.s.

HEART-BURN , s. tIkzRAgniH m., AmlapittaM, hfdayavedanA, hfdrogaH.

HEART-RENDING: (1) hfdayavidAraRaH (RA, RaM), Mu.;(2) hfdayacCid. (mfn), Ram.;(3) hfdaya- marmacCid (mfn.), U.; and sim. comp.s.

HEART-RENDING , a. marmmaBedI -dinI -di (n), marmmaCedI &c., hfdayaBedI &c., hfdayaBid m. f. n., hfdayAvid m. f. n. (D), marmmaspfk m. f. n. (S), marmmapIqAkaraH -rI -raM, cittapIqAjanakaH -kA -kaM, cittodvegajanakaH -kA -kaM, manoduHKakArI -riRI -ri (n).
HEART-ROBBING , a. manoharaH -rA -raM, manohArI -riRI -ri (n), citta- hArI &c., cittApahArI &c., cittahft m. f. n., hfdayagrAhI -hiRI -hi (n).
HEART-SICK , a. AturacittaH -ttA -ttaM, udvignamanAH -nAH -naH (s), vimanAH &c.
HEART-SORE , s. manovyaTA, manaHpIqA, hfdayapIqA, manoduHKaM.
HEART-STRINGS , s. hftpiRqaparigataM SirAdi.

HEART-WOUNDED , a. kzatahfdayaH -yA -yaM, BinnahfdayaH -yA -yaM, BinnamarmmA -rmmA -rmma (n), vidDamarmmA &c., vidDahfdayaH -yA -yaM.
HEART-WOUNDING , a. marmmaBedI -dinI -di (n), hfdayaBedI &c., hfdayAvid m. f. n. (D).

HELL , s. (Region under the earth, or residence of the Nāgas, Asuras, Daityas, &c., and not to be confounded with Naraka or the place of punishment) pAtAlaM, aDoBuvanaM, nAga- lokaH. There are seven of these Pātālas or lower regions, saptapAtAlaM. These are, 1. atalaM, 2. vitalaM, 3. pAtAlaM, 4. rasA- talaM, 5. mahAtalaM, 6. sutalaM, 7. talAtalaM. — (Place of punishment after death) narakaH, nirayaH, nArakaH. The Naraka, or Tar- tarus of the Hindūs, is divided into numerous different places of torture; such as, ‘the place paved with swords,’ asipatraM; ‘the place where the leaves of the trees are swords,’ asipatravanaM; ‘the place of great darkness,’ anDatA- misraM; ‘a place in which the wicked are baked like pots,’ taptakumBaH, kumBIpAkaH; ‘the place of burning sand,’ taptabAlukaH &c., see under HELL, p. 340; ‘abiding in h.,’ narakavAsaH; ‘descending to h.,’ aDaHpatanaM, aDogatiH f., narakapatanaM; ‘judge of h.,’ yamaH; ‘his messenger,’ yamadUtaH; ‘road to h.,’ naraka- sArgaH, aDaHpaTaH, DUmramArgaH; ‘punishment of h.,’ yamadaRqaH; ‘pit of h.,’ narakakuRqaM. Eighty-six of these pits are enumerated.

HERE: I In this place:(1) atra,(2) iha. Ph.: who is h.: kaH ko'tra BoH. Sa.; look h. is the queen: paSyeyaM devI, Ra.; h. are we: iBe smaH, Sa.II In this world:(1) iha;(2) ihaloke. Ph.: h. and hereafter: uBayatra, Ki. or paratroha ca, R. or ihA- mutra ca, S. p. H.....there:(1) itaH.......itaH, h. a flock of deer, there a herd of wild elephants: ito mfgakadambakaM, ito vanagajyUTam, K.;(2) kvacit... kvacit, R. H. and there:(1) itastataH, sang h.: itastato jagatuH, R.;(2) antarAntarA (at intervals), K.;(3) kvacit kvacit, N. (= 2).

HIATUS , s. vicCedaH, CedaH, CidraM, BedaH, BaNgaH, antaraM.

(guhyate), gup in pass. (gupyate), tiraskf in pass. (-kriyate), rahas (nom. rahAyate); ‘hidden behind the bushes,’ viwapAntaritaH -tA -taM.
HIDDEN: (1) gUQa (f. QA), ni-;(2) pracCanna (f. nA): v. Secret.

Hide, s. carman n., ajinaM, dftiH, kftti f., paSu-carman n. -tvac f.; ‘h(ide)-bound’ dfQamuzwi, kfpaRa; avaSya, avinaya, kaWora, kaWina. v. t. pracCad 10, guh 1 U, gup 1 P, aMtarDA 3 U, tiroDA, sTag 10, apavf c.; See Conceal. v. i. guh-gup pass., gupta-nilIna a. BU 1 P, ni-lI 4 A, tiroBU, tiroDA pass.; ‘h(ide)s behind the bushes’ viwa-pAMtaritastizWati-Bavati. [Hid]ing, s. gopanaM, gupti f., pracCAdanaM, sTaganaM, tiroDAnaM; ‘h(iding)-place’ niBfta-gUQa-sTAnaM, guptiH, niBftaM.
HIDE (subs.): carman (n.): v. Skin.

HIDE (v. t.): pracCAdayati (Cad, c. 10.), I will h. (the body) with these leaves: SuzkaparRapuwena pracCAdayAmi, Mr. viii.; and who h. them (thieves): ye ca pracCAdayanti tAn, Mat.: v. Also to conceal. Ph.: he hid himself under the bed: paryaNkatale niBftaM sTitaH, H. iii.; h. ing among the amaranths: kuravakErapavAritaSarIraH (rA, raM), Sa. iii.; it was not known where he hid himself: na jYAyate kApi pralInaH saH.

To HIDE , v. a. guh (c. 1. gUhati -te, gUhituM, goQuM), niguh, viniguh, Cad (c. 10. CAdayati -yituM), AcCad, samAcCad, pracCad, praticCad, saYCad, gup (c. 1. gopAyati, goptuM or in des. jugupsate -psituM), sTag (c. 10. sTagayati -yituM), antarDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), tiroDA, apiDA, piDA, upaniDA, apavf (c. 10. -vArayati -yituM), saMvf, gopanaM kf, nihnu (c. 2. -hnute -hnotuM).
To HIDE , v. n. guptaH -ptA -ptaM BU, antaritaH -tA -taM BU, gup in pass. (gupyate), tiraskf in pass. (-kriyate); ‘he hides behind the bushes,’ viwapAntarito Bavati.

High, a. ucca, unnata, ucCrita, samucCrita, socCrAya, tuMga, prAMSu, udagra, uttuMga, udgata, unnamra, UrDva. 2 uttama, viSizwa, muKya, SrezWa, parama, agrya, mahA-praDAna- in comp.; See Principal. 3 pracaMqa, tIkzRa, tIvra, balavat, tarasvin, prabala; See Strong. 4 udAtta, uttAla; ‘a h(igh) tone’ udAttaH, ucca-tAra-svaraH, tAraH. 5 (‘Of h(igh) rank’) viSizwa, utkfzwa, utkfzwa-viSizwa-padasTa, uttama-parama-padaBAj, labDapratizWa, pratipattimat, sagOrava. 6 (‘Of h(igh) family’) kulIna, mahAkula, aBijAta, aBijanavat, kulaja, mahAkulaprasUta. 7 garvodData, darpADmAta, sAvalepa, garvita, avalipta, utsikta. 8 gahana; ‘h(igh) water’ pra-vfdDA velA; ‘it is h(igh) noon’ (naBasaH) maDyamalaMkaroti BAnuH; ‘h(igh) and low’ uccAvaca, aDarottara, uttamADama, unnatAnata, natonnata, nimnonnata; ‘h(igh)er and h(igh)er’ aDikADikaM, uttarottaraM; ‘h(igh) price’ mahAmUlya; ‘h(igh) ground’ unnataBUH; ‘as h(igh) as’ mAtra (trI f.) dva-yasa (sI f.), daGna (GnI f.) in comp.; ‘he has a h(igh) opinion of you’ sa tvAM bahu ma-nyate. adv. uccEH, uccaM, ati-su pr.; UrDvaM, upari, uttamaM, paramaM; ‘on h(igh)’ UrDvaM, upari; ‘from on h(igh)’ uparizwAt; ‘the sea runs h(igh)’ balavatkzubDaH sAgaraH. ‘H(igh)-birth’ kulInatA, kulotkarzaH, ABijAtyaM; ‘h(igh)-blest’ atipuRyavat, mahABAga, atiDanya, paramasuKaBAj; ‘h(igh)-blown’ atyucCUna, ati-sPIta; ‘h(igh)-born’ kulIna, mahAkula-jAta-prasUta, aBijAta, sujAta, aBijanavat, sadvaMSya, SrezWa-uttama-kulodBava; ‘h(igh)-bred’ kulIna, SizwAcAra, sujana, suSIla, sadBAvaviSizwa, sOjanyopeta, sadAcAra, sADuvftta; ‘h(igh)-built’ socCrAya, ucca; ‘h(igh)-day’ utsavadinaM, udDarza-divasaH; ‘h(igh)-fed’ atipuzwa, hfzwapuzwa; ‘h(igh)-flying’ aparimita; ‘h(igh)-hand’ OdDatyaM, garvaH, uddAmatvaM; niryaMtraRatvaM; ‘h(igh)-handed’ udData, sagarva, uddAma, aniyaMtraRa, ucCfMKala, svErin; ‘h(igh)-hung’ UrDvabadDa; ‘h(igh)-land’ aDityakA, unnataBUmi f.; (a.) parvatIya, unnataH ‘h(igh)-lander’ parvatIyaH, parvatavAsin m.; ‘h(igh)-mettled’ mahAsattva, urusattva, ojasvin, adInacitta, tejasvin; garvita, atimadAnvita; ‘h(igh)-minded’ mahA-tman, mahAmanaska, udAra-DI-cetas-carita, mahecCa, mahASaya; ‘h(igh)-principled’ sADu-caritra, puRyAtman, puRyaSIla; ‘h(igh)-priest’ purohitADyakzaH; ‘h(igh)-prized’ mahAmUlya, mahArGa, bahumata; ‘h(igh)-red’ GanAruRa, atirakta; ‘h(igh)-road, -street, -way’ rAjamArgaH-paTaH, mahApaTaH-mArgaH, GaMwApaTaH, saMsaraRaM, raTyA, vi-SiKA, pratolI; ‘h(igh)-seasoned’ suvAsita; ‘h(igh)-spirited’ mahA-uru-sattva, adInavftti, ojasvin, Urjita,

HIGH (adj.): (1) uccaH (ccA, ccaM) or uccEH (indec.). h. places: uccEH sTAnAni, D.; but now a h. er (place) than that on account of your favour of remembrance: adya tUccE staraM tAByAM smaraRAnugrahAttava, Ku. vi. 19.; much more one so h. (i.e. noble: q.v.) kiM punaryastaToccEH, Me. 1. 17.; h. -minded: uccamanaskaH (skA, skaM); of a h. family, h.-born: uccavaMSajaH (jA, jaM); at a h. price: uccamUlyena; h. talk: uccapralApaH, D.: v. Haughty; h. education: uccaSikzA (after Bengali);(2) unnataH (tA, taM), sam- (= lofty), h. summit: unnataM SElAgram, M. n.; connected with that h. (personage): unnatena tena yojitasambanDaH (nDA, nDaM), Ku. vi. 30.;(3) ucCritaH (tA, taM), sam-, (lit. =h.; fig. =lofty: rare), h. umbrella: ucCritaM cCatram, R. xvii. 33.; six feet h.: caturhastocCritaH (tA, taM); h. sound: samucCrito ravaH, Ku.;(4) tuNga (f. NgA), ud-, (= 3: rare), even a h. mountain is accessible: gamyastuNgo'pi BUGaraH, Ki. xi. 63,;(5) prAMSu (mfn.) (= tall: q.v.); (6) mahat (f. tI) (when h. =great), h. plea- sure: mahAsuKam; h. admiral: *mahAnAvikanAyakaH; h. priest: *mahAn purohitaH: v. Also chief. Ph.: h. note: udAttasvaraH; h. wind: gurusamIraH, Ku.; it is h. noon: maDyamalaNkaroti BAnuH; h. time: samucitakAlaH; h. water: pravfdDA velA; h. meat: ugramAMsam; h. anti- quity: atipUrvakAlaH; h. sauce: ugropaskaraH; h. er and h. er: aDikADikam (= more and more); h. est: i.e. extreme: q.v.: paraH (rA, raM); h. treason: rAjadrohaH, -aparADaH; he has h. opinion of you: sa tvAmuccErmanyate; on h. UrdDam; from on h.: uparizwAt.
HIGH (adv.): I Lit.:(1) uccEH;(2) uccakEH; (3) uccam.II Fig.: expr. by adj.: h. -aimed: uccABilAzin (f. RI).

HIGH , a. (Lofty) uccaH -ccA -ccaM, unnataH -tA -taM, ucCritaH -tA -taM, samunnataH -tA -taM, samucCritaH -tA -taM, aByucCritaH -tA -taM, socCrAyaH -yA -yaM, ucCrAyI -yiRI -yi (n), prAMSuH -SuH -Su, tuNgaH -NgA -NgaM, uttuNgaH -NgA -NgaM, udagraH -grA -graM, udgataH -tA -taM, unnamraH -mrA -mraM, UrdDvaH -rdDvA -rdDvaM, uttaraH -rA -raM, uttamaH -mA -maM, dIrGaH -rGA -rGaM; ‘a high tree,’ uccataruH m., dIrGataruH. — (Elevated in rank) utkfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, utkfzwapadasTaH -sTA -sTaM, prati- pattimAn -matI -mat (t), uttamapadasTaH -sTA -sTaM, anavamaH -mA -maM, anIcaH -cA -caM. — (Noble, of high family) mahAkulaH -lA -laM -lInaH -nA -naM. — (Haughty) garvvI -rvviRI -rvvi (n), garvvodDataH -tA -taM, unnatacetAH -tAH -taH (s), unnadDacetAH &c., udDataH -tA -taM, samudDataH -tA -taM, utsiktaH -ktA -ktaM. — (Capital, great, chief) uttamaH -mA -maM, paramaH -mA -maM, muKyaH -KyA -KyaM, SrezWaH -zWA -zWaM, praDAna in comp., mahA in comp. — (As sound) udAttaH -ttA -ttaM, uttAlaH -lA -laM, kalottAlaH -lA -laM; ‘a high tone,’ udAttaH, uccasvaraH, tAraH; ‘in a high tone,’ udAttasvareRa, uccEHsvareRa; ‘high and low,’ uttamADamaH -mA -maM, utkfzwApakfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, uttarADaraH -rA -raM, uccAvacaH -cA -caM, unnatAnataH -tA -taM, nimnonnataH -tA -taM; ‘the high and low,’ uttamADamO m. du., utkfzwApakfzwO m. du.; ‘very high,’ atyuccaH -ccA -ccaM; ‘higher [Page343-b+ 51] and higher,’ uttarottaraM; ‘highest,’ uttamaH -mA -maM, paramaH -mA -maM; ‘a high price,’ durmUlyaM; ‘a high wind,’ prabalavAyuH m., pracaRqa- vAyuH, ativAtaH; ‘high ground,’ unnataBUBAgaH; ‘as high as an elephant,’ gajadvayasaH -sI -saM, gajamAtraH -trI -traM, gajadaGnaH -GnI -GnaM, gajaparimARaH -RA -RaM.

(-sTApayati -yituM), upahf. — (Hold up, raise aloft) uccIkf, uccEH kf, UrdDvIkf, unnam (c. 10. -namayati -yituM), ucCri (c. 1. -Crayati -yituM), udyam. — (Hold up, sustain) Df, sanDf, Alamb (c. 1. -lambate, c. 10. -lambayati -yituM), avalamb, samavalamb, uttamB (c. 10. -tamBayati -yituM, rt. stamB), Bf. — (Hold one's tongue) jihvAM rakz or Df.
