HOLY: puRGa (f. RyA), h. person: puRyajanaH, Ki. iii. 31.; h. prayer: puRyA stutiH, K.; h. rivers: saritaH puRyAH, Ram. ii. 12. 5.; h. place of pilgrimage: puRyatIrTaH, Ram.; h. land: pURyaBUmiH: v. Also pure, sacred. Ph.: h. father, mother: Bagavat (f. tI); “h. alliance”: DarmasanDiH; h. -day: v. Holiday.

HOLY , a. puRyaH -RyA -RyaM, puRyavAn -vatI -vat (t), puRyaSIlaH -lA -laM, puRyAtmA -tmA -tma (n), pavitraH -trA -traM, DarmmaSIlaH -lA -laM, SuciH -ciH -ci, SucimanAH -nAH -naH (s), SucivrataH -tA -taM, vimalaH -lA -laM, amalAtmA -tmA -tma (n), nirmmalAntaHkaraRaH -RA -RaM, SudDamatiH -tiH -ti, pavitramatiH -tiH -ti, SudDAtmA &c., SudDahfdayaH -yA -yaM, DArmmikaH -kI -kaM, sADuH -DuH -DvI -Du; ‘holy land,’ puRyaBUmiH f., puRyaBUH f.; ‘holy writ,’ SrutiH f.; ‘holy place of pilgrimage,’ tIrTaH -rTaM, puRyatIrTaM, kzetraM, puRyasTAnaM.
HOLY-WATER , s. puRyajalaM, puRyodakaM, puRyAmbu n., puRyavAri n.

HOLYDAY , s. (Sacred day) puRyAhaM, puRyadinaM, puRyadivasaH. — (Festival) utsavaH, utsavadinaM, parvvAhaH, udDarzadinaM, AnandadivasaH, yAtrA, rAserasaH. — (Day on which there is intermission of study) anaDyAyaH anaDyAyadivasaH, anaDyAyamahotsavaH, asvADyAyatiTiH m. f., viSrAma- divasaH; ‘holyday folk,’ yAtrAjanaH, yAtrAlokaH.

Homage, s. namaskAraH, aBivaMdanaM, praRAmaH, praRati f., pUjA, arcanaM, upAsanA, praRipAtaH, sevAMjaliH; sevA, AdaraH, praBuBakti f.; ‘pay or do h(omage)’ praRam 1 P, vaMd 1 A, praRipat 1 P; See Bow.

HOMAGE (subs.): I In gen.(1) namaskAraH; (2) namasyA, N.: v. Also respect. To do, pay h.: namati, pra-, (nam, c. 1.), men do not pay h. to a man until he pays h. to you: na namanti puruzaM puruzAstava yAvadISa na natiH kriyate, Ki.II Feudal: to do h. (to a lord): perh. praButvaM svIkaroti.

HOMAGE , s. pUjA, praRAmaH, praRatiH f., praRipAtaH -patanaM, arcanaM -nA, arcA, aByarcA, aByarcanaM, namaskAraH, mAnaM, sammAnaM, satkAraH, pAdavandanaM, sevA, sevAYjaliH m., AdaraH, BaktiH f., praBuktiH f., pratItiH f., vinItiH f., upAsanA, SevaM.

To HOMAGE , v. a. pUj (c. 10. pUjayati -yituM), sampUj, arc (c. 1. arcati -rcituM, c. 10. arcayati -yituM), praRipat (c. 1. -patati -tituM), upas (c. 2. -Aste -AsituM), praRam (c. 1. -Ramati -RantuM), satkf; ‘he paid homage,’ praRatavAn.
HOMAGER , s. pUjakaH, praRAmakft m., praRipAtakArI m. (n), sammAnakft m.

Home, s. gfhaM, vAsaH, vAsasTAnaM-BUmi f., svagfhaM, sva or nija-gehaM-deSaH-vAsaH-sTAnaM-BavanaM; See House; ‘devoted to h(ome)’ gfhAsaktacitta. adv. gfhaM, gfhaM prati; ‘the words went h(ome) to his heart’ tadvacaH tasya hfdayamarmAspfSat; ‘touching h(ome)’ marmaspfS-Bid; ‘goes h(ome) to me’ mAmeva lakzIkaroti (S. 7); ‘h(ome)-born’ gfhajAta; ‘h(ome)-bound’ gfhagAmin; ‘h(ome)-bred’ gfhaja-jAta, gfhya; ‘h(ome)-made’ gfhanirmita, gfhotpanna; ‘h(ome)-sick’ gfhavirahArta; ‘h(ome)-stall, -stead’ gfhaM, vAsaH; veSmaBUH, vAstu m. n. [Home]less, a. nirAlaya, nirASraya, nirgfha. [Home]ly, a. gfhya, gfhaja. 2 grAmya, grAmIRa-ya, aSizwa, prAkfta, asaBya, aSlIla, asaMskfta. adv. grAmyavat, asaByatayA, aSizwaprakAreRa. [Home]ward, adv. gfhABimuKaM, aBigfhaM.

HOME (subs.): (1) gfham (= house: q.v.), gone h.: gfhaM gataH, Mr. ix.;(2) janmaBUmiH (= birth- -place), where is your h., sir? Madam, Patna is my h.: kuta AryaH? Arye pAwaliputraM me janmaBUmiH, Mr. ii.;(3) AlayaH (= abode: q.v.). Ph.: at h.: gfhe or gehe, U. i. 57. 8.; he is making himself at h. there: tatrA paricita iva vyavaharati.
HOME (adv.): I Lit.: gfham.II Fig: expr. by marman (n.), to come h.: marma spfSati.
HOME (adj.): I Lit.: grha- in comp.II Of one's country: “h. department”. *svadeSaviBAgaH.

HOME , s. svagfhaM, gfhaM, svasTAnaM, svadeSaH, svavAsaH, svavizayaH, svagehaH, svaveSma n. (n), nijagfhaM, nijAlayaH, nijagehaH, svaBavanaM, svanilayaH; ‘devoted to home,’ gfhArUQacetAH -tAH -taH (s).
HOME , adv. gfhaM prati, svagfhaM prati; ‘he went home,’ gfhaM yayO. — (Close) nikawe; ‘speech that strikes home,’ saNgatavAkyaM, hfdayaNgamavAkyaM.
HOME-BORN , a. gfhajAtaH -tA -taM, svagfhajaH -jA -jaM, svadeSajaH -jA -jaM; ‘home-born slave,’ gfhajAto dAsaH, jYAtidAsaH.
HOME-BOUND: (1) gfhagAmin (f. nI);(2) svadeSa- gAmin (f. nI).
HOME-BRED: I Lit.: gfhajaH (jA, jaM) or jAtaH (tA, taM).II Rude: grAmya (f. myA).
HOME-BRED , a. gfhajaH -jA -jaM, gfhyaH -hyA -hyaM, AntarveSmikaH -kI -kaM.
HOME-FELT , a. antarasTaH -sTA -sTaM, antaratamaH -mA -maM, antarBUtaH -tA -taM.
HOME-MADE: I Made at home: gfha- in comp., h. butter: gfhanavanItam.II Made in one's own country: svadeSa- in comp.: v. Also made.
HOME-MADE , a. gfhanirmmitaH -tA -taM, gfhakftaH -tA -taM, gfhotpannaH -nnA -nnaM.
HOME-SPUN , a. gfhajAtaH -tA -taM, gfhajaH -jA -jaM, gfhyaH -hyA -hyaM.
HOME-STALL or HOME-STEAD, s. gfhaM, vAsasTAnaM, vasatiH f., AvAsaH
HOMELESS: agfhaH (hA, haM), Mah. iii. 27. 16.; nirASrayaH (yA, yaM) and sim. comp.s.: v. Also exile.
HOMELESS , a. nirAlayaH -yA -yaM, nirAspadaH -dA -daM, nirASrayaH -yA -yaM.
HOMELINESS , s. grAmyatA, grAmIyatvaM, gfhyatA, asaByatA, nIcatA, aSlIlatA, aSudDatvaM, aSizwatvaM.
HOMELY: I Domestic: q.v.: gfhya (f. hyA). II Plain, unpolished: grAmya (f. myA).

HOMELY , a. grAmyaH -myA -myaM, grAmikaH -kI -kaM, grAmIyaH -yA -yaM, grAmIRaH -RA -RaM, gfhyaH -hyA -hyaM, gfhajaH -jA -jaM, prAkftaH -tI -taM, asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, aSlIlaH -lA -laM, nIcaH -cA -caM, aDamaH -mA -maM, aSudDaH -dDA -dDaM, aSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, asaMskftaH -tA -taM, aparizkftaH -tA -taM; ‘homely speech,’ grAmyaM.
HOMELY , adv. grAmyaM, grAmyaprakAreRa, asaByaM, nIcaM, gfhyatas.
HOMER: I The poet: *homaraH.II A measure: mAnaviSezaH.
HOMESICK: gfhavirahAturaH (rA, raM); gfhavirahArta (f. rtA), etc.
HOMESPUN: I Adj.: gfhotaH (tA, taM) (?).II Subs.: gfhotam (?); gfhanirmitavastram.
HOMESTALL, HOMESTEAD: (1) vAstu (mn.); (2) gfhavAstu (n.), Kat;(3) veSman (n.) (rare) Kat.;(4) vAsaBUmiH, Mit.
HOMEWARD: svadeSABimuKam, “H. -bound”. svadeSABi- muKaH (KA, KaM): v. Also home-bound.
HOMEWARD , adv. gfhaM prati, svavAsaM prati, svasTAnaM prati.
HOMICIDAL , a. nfhatyAkArI -riRI -ri (n), manuzyaGAtI -tinI -ti (n).
Homicide, s. nfhatyA, manuzyavaDaH. 2 (Person) manuzyaGAtin m., nfhaMtf m., manuzyaGAtakaH. [Homicid]al, a. nfGAtin.
HOMICIDE: I The deed: nfhatyA and sim. comp.s.: v. Murder.II The slayer: (1) narahatyAkArin (f. RI);(2) manuzyaGAtin (f. nI).
HOMICIDE , s. nfhatyA, manuzyahatyA, manuzyabaDaH, manuzyaGAtaH. — (One who kills a man) nfhantA m. (ntf), manuzyaGAtakaH.
Homily, s. DarmavAkyaM.
HOMILY: DarmaprabanDaH (?): v. Sermon.
HOMILY , s. pUjASAlAsu SrAvaRIyaM DarmmavizayaM vAkyaM.
HOMLINESS: grAmyatA: v. Homely.
HOMOEPATHIC: expr. by comp., h. doctor: *samavyavasTAvidvEdyaH.
HOMOEPATHY: *samavyavasTA, samavyavasTASAstram.
Homogeneal, Homogeneous, a. samAna-jAti-jAtIya, sa-eka-jAti, savarRa, eka-sa-Darman, samAna-BAva, eka-sa-jAtIya; ‘h(omogeneous) vowels’ savarRAH.
HOMOGENEAL, HOMOGENEOUS: *sajAtIyaH (yA, yaM).

HOMOGENEAL , HOMOGENEOUS, a. samAnajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, sajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, samAnajAtiH -tiH -ti, sajAtiH -tiH -ti, samaBAvaH -vA -vaM, samAna- BAvaH -vA -vaM, samaDarmmA -rmmA -rmma (n), ekajAtiH -tiH -ti, ekaDarmmA &c., svaBAvIyaH -yA -yaM.
HOMOGENEALNESS , HOMOGENEITY, HOMOGENEOUSNESS, s. samAnajAtitA, sajAtitA, BAvasamatA, BAvasamAnatA, jAtisamatA.
Homologous, a. tulya-sama-parimARa.
HOMOLOGOUS: *samasTiti (mfn.).
HOMOLOGOUS , a. tulyAkAraH -rA -raM, tulyaparimARaH -RA -RaM, samaparimARaH -RA -RaM.
Homonym, BinnArTaH SabdaH; ‘a collection of h(omonym)s’ BinnArTavargaH. [Homonym]ous, a. BinnArTa, anekArTa.
HOMONYMOUS: bahvarTakaH (kA, kaM): v. Also equivocal.
HOMONYMOUS , a. BinnArTaH -rTA -rTaM, sandigDArTaH -rTA -rTaM, dvyarTaH -rTA -rTaM. [Page348-a+ 51] samasaMjYakaH -kA -kaM, samanAmA -mA -ma (n).
HOMONYMY , s. BinnArTatA, viBinnArTatA, arTaBedaH, dvyarTatA, nAmasamatA.
Hone, s. SARaH, SARASman m.
HONE: SARaH(naH): v. Whetstone.
HONE , s. SARaH -RI, SARASma n. (n), SAnaH, kzuraDArAtejanaprastaraH.

Honest, a. Suci, fju, sarala, amAyin, dakziRa, akuwila, ajihma, SudDamati-BAva, SudDAtman, akapawa, nizkapawa, nirvyAja, nirvyalIka, avyAja, vimalAtman, daMBahIna, nyAyya, nyAyyAcAra, saccarita, nyAyavartin, sADuvftta-SIla, sADu, prAMjala, satyavftta, satyaSIla, satyavAdin. 2 avitaTa, satya, akftrima, akftaka; See Frank also; ‘h(onest) gains’ nyAyArjitaM; ‘h(onest) statement’ nirvyAjaM vacanaM. [Honest]ly, adv. saralaM, nyAyena, nyAyataH, SucitayA, nizkapawaM, nirvyAjaM, amAyayA, nirvyalIkaM. [Honest]y, s. Su-citA, ArjavaM, nizkApawyaM, sAralyaM, akO-wilyaM, dAkziRyaM, amAyayA, akapawaM, avyAjaH, SudDaBAvaH, vEmalyaM, nirvyalIkatA, ajihmatA, satyatA, akftakatA; ‘h(onesty) is the best policy’ BAvaSudDiH eva sADizWA AcAra-saraRiH, sAralyaM sattamo mArgaH.

HONEST: I Decent, good: q.v.II Upright, just:(1) Suci (mfn.) (= pure), M.;(2) arTaSOcayukta (f. ktA), K. b.;(3) saralaH (lA, laM) (= simple);(4) nizkapawaH (wA, waM) (=guile- -less).III Frank, sincere: q.v.

HONEST , a. (Upright, just) saralaH -lA -laM, dakziRaH -RA -RaM, SuciH -ciH -ci, nyAyAcAraH -rA -raM, nyAyavarttI -rttinI -rtti (n), nyAyyaH -yyA -yyaM, fjuH -juH -ju, saccaritaH -tA -taM, sAttvikaH -kI -kaM, SudDamatiH -tiH -ti, SudDAtmA -tmA -tma (n), ajihmaH -hmA -hmaM, akuwilaH -lA -laM, aSaWaH -WA -WaM, aSaWaDIH -DIH -Di, mAyAhInaH -nA -naM, amAyaH -yA -yaM -yikaH -kI -kaM, akapawaH -wA -waM, nizkapawaH -wA -waM, kapawahInaH -nA -naM, nirvyAjaH -jA -jaM, vimalAtmA -tmA -tma (n), nirvyalIkaH -kA -kaM, avakraH -krA -kraM, DArmmikaH -kI -kaM, damBarahitaH -tA -taM, DarmmakArI -riRI -ri (n), BadraH -drA -draM, sADuH -DuH -DvI -Du, san satI -sat (t), uttamaH -mA -maM, saralayAyI -yinI -yi (n), SlakzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, prAYjalaH -lA -laM, praguRaH -RA -RaM. — (True) satyaH -tyA -tyaM, satyakaH -kA -kaM, satyaSIlaH -lA -laM, satyavfttaH -ttA -ttaM, satyavAdI -dinI -di (n).
HONESTLY: (1) CalaM vihAya;(2) nizkapawam: v. Also simply, sincerely.
HONESTLY , adv. saralaM, sAralyena, nyAyena, nyAyatas, nyAyyaM, nizkapawaM, kapawaM vinA, nirvyAjaM, nirvyalIkaM, amAyayA, mAyAM vinA, saralavat, Sucivat, ajihyaM, sadAkziRyaM.
HONESTY: (1) arTaSOcaB or sim. SOcam or SucitA, tvam (when the sense is clear);(2) nizkapawatA (= guilelessness);(3) sAralyam (=simplicity); (4) Arjavam (= uprightness).

HONESTY , s. sAralyaM, saralatA, dAkziRyaM, SucitA -tvaM, fjutA, ArjavaM, amAyA, mAyAhInatA, akapawaH, akApawyaM, kapawahInatA, avyAjaH, nyAyitA, nyAyAcAratA, ajihyatA, akOwilyaM, aSaWatA, nirvyalIkatA, avakratA, asteyaM, apESunaM, BadratA, sADutA, SudDatvaM, DArmmikatvaM, satyatA, satyaSI- latA, satyavAditvaM, nErmalyaM, vimalatA, adattAnupAdAnaM.

Honey, s. maDu n., kzOdraM, mAkzikaM, sAraGaM; ‘h(oney) of flowers’ puzpAsavaM, puzparasaH-sAraH, kusumamaDu; ‘h(oney)-bee’ maDumakzikA, saraGA; ‘h(oney)-comb’ maDukoSaH, karaMqaH; ‘h(oney)-moon’ AnaMdamAsaH; ‘h(oney)-tongued’ maDuraBAzin, maDuravAc. v. t. maDurIkf 8 U. v. i. upa-lal 10; See Fawn. [Honey]ed, a. maDumaDura, suDA-syaMdin, maDura.

HONEY: maDu (n.), h. -bees make h. by gathering the juice of divers trees: BaDukaramakzikA nAnAjAtInAM vfkzARAM rasAn samAhftya maDu nizpAdayanti, S. c.; old (h.) is binding and astringent: purARaM grAhakaM rUkzaM, Bha; of this (king) who is h. in mouth and poison at heart: asya muKamaDorhf dayavizasya, Sa. v.

HONEY , s. maDu n., kzOdraM, puzpaniryAsaH, puzparasaH, puzpasAraH, puzpAsavaM, kusu- mAsavaM, mAkzikaM, CAtraM, -trakaM, sAraGaM, kApiSAyanaM; ‘honey of flowers,’ savaM; ‘become honey,’ maDusAdBUtaH -tA -taM.
To HONEY , v. n. maDuravacoBiH or maDuravAkyEH sAntv (c. 10. sAntvayati -yituM).
HONEY , s. (Of flowers) suDA. HOOD, (Of snake) darvI, sPawA.
HONEY-BEE: maDumakzikA: v. Bee.
HONEY-COMB , s. maDukozaH, maDuvAsaH, maDucakraM, mAkzikASrayaM, maDukramaH, karaRqaH.
HONEY-HARVEST: maDusaMgrahaH (?) and sim. comp.s.
HONEY-MOON , s. AnandamAsaH, vivAhAt paraM praTamamAso yasmin strIpuruzO premamAtraM kurutaH.
HONEY-SUCKLE , s. suraBiganDaviSizwo latAviSezaH.
HONEY-SWEET , a. maDuraH -rA -raM, maDuvat svAduH -duH -dvI -du, maDusAt ind.
HONEY-TONGUED: (1) muKamaDu (mfn.), Sa. and sim. comp.s.;(2) perh. maDujihva (f. hnA).
HONEY-TONGUED , a. maDuraBAzI -ziRI -zi (n), maDuravAdI -dinI -di (n).
HONEYCOMB: (1) maDukozaH;(2) maDucakram;(3) Catrakam;(4) maDujAlakam, Si. xii. 54;(5) kzOdrapawalam (rare), R.
HONEYDEW: dAlaM maDu, Bha.
HONEYED: maDumayaH (yI, yaM) (lit. and fig.) and sim. comp.s.
HONEYSUCKLE: *maDugarBA; supuzpalatABedaH.
HONIED , a. maDumAn -matI -mat (t), maDumayaH -yI -yaM, maDuraH -rA -raM.

Honor, v. t. pUj 10, arc 1 P, 10, man c., saMBU c., satkf 8 U, puraskf, mah 1 P, 10, Adf 6 A. 2 sev 1 A, Sru desid. (SuSrUzate), ArAD c.; ‘h(onor)ed the invitation’ nimaMtraRamAdriyata, sagOravaM svIcakAra. 3 anugrah 9 P, prasad 1 P (with loc.). s. mAnaH, saMmAnaH, pUjA, arcanaM, arhaRA, saMBAvanA, AdaraH, satkAraH. 2 sevA, SuSrUzA, ArADanaM. 3 KyAti f., kIrti f., yaSas n., pratizWA, gO-ravaM, pratipatti f., utkarzaH, utkfzwa-praDAna-padaM, unnati f.; kulInatA, ABijAtyaM, prADAnyaM, SrezWatvaM; ‘your or his h(onor)’ atra-tatra-BavAn; Bavat. [Honor]able, a. pUjya, mAnya, mAnanIya, pU-jArha, AdaraRIya. 2 su-pra-vi-KyAta, viSruta, suprasidDa, pratipattimat, mahAyaSas. 3 yaSaskara-kIrtikara (rI f.), pratizWAvaha, SlAGya, praSa-sya, mAnada, gOravAnvita. 4 kulIna, aBijAta, mahAkula, udAracitta-carita; See Noble. 5 Suci, nyAyyAcAra, saccarita, sADuvftta, pu-RyAtman, Sucivrata; See Honest. [Honor]ary, a. mAnada, kIrtikara, yaSaskara, praSasya. 2 alABa-kara, mAnamAtradAyin. Honorably, adv. samAnaM, sagOravaM, SlAGyaprakAreRa, praSaMsApUrvaM, suyaSasA, pratizWApUrvaM. 2 Sucivat, DArmikatayA, fjutayA, saralatayA, nyAyataH.
Honorarium, s. dakziRA.
HONORARY: no equiv. *sABmAnikaH (kI, kaM) or by circumlo.

HONORARY , a. sammAnakaraH -rA -raM, mAnadaH -dA -daM, yaSasyaH -syA -syaM, yaSasvI -svinI -svi (n), kIrttikaraH -rA -raM, yaSaskaraH. — (Confer- ring honour only, without gain) sammAnamAtradaH -dA -daM, kIrtti- mAtrakaraH -rI -raM alABakaraH -rI -raM.

HONOUR (subs.): I A nice sense of what is right: mAnaH, sam-, who has from age lost all sense of h.: jarAvaluptamAnAvamAnacittaH, D. ii.II Nobility, chastity: mAnaH, sama-, rich in h.: mAna- DanaH (nA, naM), Ki. ii. 19.; devoid of h.: mAnahInaH (nA, naM), Ki. xi. 59.III Respect, reverence: q.v.(1) mAnaH, sama-, P.;(2) AdaraH (= atten- -tion):IV A mark of respect:(1) mAnaH, sam-, for this h.: asya saBmAnasya kfte, P. i. 3.; (2) gOravam, master's h.s on dependents are as a rule moving with the object to be accomplished: prayojanApekzitayA praBURAM prAyaScalaM gOravamASritezu, Ku. iii. 1.;(3) prasAdaH (= favour: q.v.).

HONOUR (v.): (1) mAnayati, saM-, (rarely) prati-, (c. of man), yet your Highness will be pleased to h. my request: taTApi madvijYApanAM mAnayitumarhatyAryaH, Mu. ii.;(2) pUjayati, sam-, aBi-, pra-, (pvaj, c. 10.) (= to respect: q.v.) he, although destitute of h. will be everywhere h. ed: sammAna- hIno'pi sa sarvatra prapUjyate, P. i. 3.

HONOUR , s. (Fame, reputation) kIrttiH f., yaSas n., KyAtiH f., suKyAtiH f., viKyAtiH f., pratizWA, viSrutiH f., samAKyA, pratipattiH f. — (Reverence) sammAnaM, mAnaM, pUjA, arcanaM -nA, arcA, aByarcA -rcanaM, namaskAraH, sevA, arhA, arhaRaM -RA, AdaraH, samBAvanA, satkAraH, ArADanaM, puraskAraH, samBramaH, SlAGA. — (Dignity, honourable rank) utkarzaH, utkfzwatA, utkfzwapadaM, kulInapadaM, pratipattiH f., praDAnapadaM, praDAnatA, prADAnyaM, SrezWatvaM, unnatiH f., maryyAdA, aBijAtatA, pUjyatA, mAnyatA -tvaM, aByarhaRI- yetA. — (Family honour) maryyAdA, kulamaryyAdA.

To HONOUR , v. a. pUj (c. 10. pUjayati -yituM), sampUj, aBipUj, man (c. 10. mAnayati -yituM), samman, pratiman, arc (c. 1. arcati -rcituM, c. 10. arcayati -yituM), aByarc, samaByarc, samarc, sev (c. 1. sevate -vituM, c. 10. sevayati -yituM), arh (c. 10. arhayati -yituM), samBU (c. 10. -BAvayati -yituM), Adf — (c. 6. -driyate -darttuM), namaskf, satkf, puraskf, ArAD (c. 10. -rADa- [Page348-b+ 51] yati -yituM), Sru in des. (SuSrUzate -zituM), aYc (c. 1. aYcati -YcituM) mah (c. 1. mahati -hituM), anugrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), pUjAM kf, sammAnaM kf. — (Accept a bill) leKyapatraM grah or svIkf or Adf.

HONOURABLE: I Possessing a high mind: mAnin (f. nI).II Illustrious, respected: (1) mAnya (f. nyA) or mAnanIyaH (yA, yaM), sam-; (2) pUjya (f. jyA) or pUjanIyaH (yA, yaM), I have been commanded by h. sir (you): pUjyenAhamAdizwaH, Mah.: v. Respectable.III Conferring honour: sammAnakaraH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s.: v. Also famous.IV Good, noble: q.v.: SudDa (f. dDA).

HONOURABLE , a. pUjyaH -jyA -jyaM, pUjanIyaH -yA -yaM, pUjayitavyaH -vyA -vyaM, sampUjanIyaH -yA -yaM, sammAnyaH -nyA -nyaM, mAnyaH -nyA -nyaM, mAnI -ninI -ni (n), pUjArhaH -rhA -rhaM, arcArhaH -rhA -rhaM, arhyaH -rhyA -rhyaM, arhaRIyaH -yA -yaM, SlAGyaH -GyA -GyaM, AdaraRIyaH -yA -yaM, puraskaraRIyaH -yA -yaM, maryyAdAvAn -vatI -vat (t), maryyAdAnvitaH -tA -taM. — (Illus- trious) KyAtaH -tA -taM, suKyAtaH -tA -taM, yaSasvI -svinI -svi (n), mahAyaSAH -SAH -SaH (s), kIrttimAn -matI -mat (t), pratipattimAn -matI -mat (t), viSrutaH -tA -taM, prasidDaH -dDA -dDaM. — (Conferring honour) kIrttikaraH -rI -raM, yaSaskaraH -rI -raM, yaSasyaH -syA -syaM. — (Upright, equitable) saccaritaH -tA -taM, nyAyAcAraH -rA -raM, DArmmikaH -kI -kaM, SuciH -ciH -ci, dakziRaH -RA -RaM, sAttvikaH -kI -kaM, SudDAtmA -tmA -tma (n), nirvyalIkaH -kA -kaM, nizkapawaH -wA -waM, vimalAtmA -tmA -tma (n), avakraH -krA -kraM, fjuH -juH -ju, sADuH -DuH -DvI -Du. — (Noble) kulInaH -nA -naM, udAraH -rA -raM, udAracetAH -tAH -taH (s).
HONOURABLY , adv. samAnaM, sammAnapUrvvaM, Sucivat, DArmmikavat, sADuvat, udAravat, sOdAryyaM, satkArapUrvvaM, namaskArapUrvvaM, SlAGyaprakAreRa, sukIrttipUrvvaM, suyaSasA, nirvyalIkaM, sampUjanIyaM.

HONOURED , p. p. pUjitaH -tA -taM, sampUjitaH -tA -taM, arcitaH -tA -taM aByarcitaH -tA -taM, sammAnitaH -tA -taM, puraskftaH -tA -taM, sevitaH -tA -taM, arhitaH -tA -taM, sevyamAnaH -nA -naM, nizevyamARaH -RA -RaM, AdftaH -tA -taM, aYcitaH -tA -taM, satkftaH -tA -taM, mahitaH -tA -taM, ArADitaH -tA -taM, SuSrUzitaH -tA -taM, aninditaH -tA -taM. — (Accepted as a bill) gfhItaH -tA -taM, svIkftaH -tA -taM, AdftaH -tA -taM; ‘to be honoured,’ pUj in pass. (pUjyate), maha (nom. mahIyate).
Hood, s. PaRA-RaH, PawA, sPowA; ‘expands the h(ood)’ PaRAM kurute (S. 6); ‘expanded h(ood)’ BogaH. 2 PaRAkfti SiraskaM. v. t. Sira-strARena piDA 3 U or prAvf 5 U.
HOOD: I For women: Siraskam (?)II Of a carriage: Siras (n.) (??).III Of a serpent: PaRA.
HOOD , s. strIvastrAnubadDaM mastakAcCAdanaM or mastakAvaraRaM or mastakapiDAnaM, PaRAkAraM mastakAcCAdanaM, SiraskaM, SirastraM -strARaM, SirovastraM; ‘of a snake,’ PaRaH -RA -RaM, BogaH, sPowA.
To HOOD , v. a. pUrvvoktapiDAnena mastakam ACad (c. 10. -CAdayati -yituM), mastrakAvaraRena piDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM).
Hoodwink, v. t. (nayane) vastreRa piDA 3 U or AcCad 10 or Avf 5 U.
HOODWINK: I Lit.: v. To blind.II To deceive: q.v.: perh. Calayati (Cal c. 10.).
To HOODWINK , v. a. cakzupI vastreRa ruD (c. 7. ruRadDi, rodDuM), nayane piDAnena Avf (c. 5. -vfRoti -varituM -rItuM) or ACad (c. 10. -CAda- yati -yituM), nayanaroDaM kf.
Hoof, s. KuraH, SaPaH-PaM, kzuraH, viMKaH, niGfzvaH. [Hoof]ed, a. Kurin, Kurayukta, SaPayukta.
HOOF: (1) KuraH, right h.: dakziRaKuraH, K.;(2) SaPa (mn.) (rare).
HOOF , s. KuraH, kzuraH, SaPaH -PaM, varttakaH -kA, niGfzvaH, puwaH, viNKaH, riNKaH; ‘hoof of a cow,’ gokzuraM, gozpadaM; ‘mark of a hoof,’ KurapadavI, KuracihnaM.
HOOFED: (1) Kurin (f. RI);(2) KurAnvitaH (tA, taM); and sim. comp.s.
HOOFED , a. KurI -riRI -ri (n), kzurI -riRI -ri (n), KurayuktaH -ktA -ktaM.

Hook, s. AkarzaRI, grahaRI, DaraRI; ‘fish-h(ook)’ baqiSaM-SA-SI, matsyaveDanI; ‘h(ook) for elephants’ aMkuSaH, Sf(sf)Ri f. v. t. baqiSena Df 1 P or grah 9 U. [Hook]ed, a. vakra, kuwila, kuMcita, aMkuSAkAra, jihma; See Crooked.
HOOK (v.): I Of fishes: vaqiSayati (nomi.). II To entrap: pASe pAtayati, (c. of pat).
HOOK (subs.): I Fish-h.: q.v.: vaqiSam.II To goad elephants: aNkuSa (mn.).III In gen.: AkarzaRI (?).IV A sickle: dAtram.V Fig.: pASaH: v. Snare.

HOOK , s. (Any thing bent that catches hold) AkarzI -rziRI, aNkuSaH, AkarzaRArTaM vakrayantraM or vakralohaH, grahaRI, DaraRI. — (Fish- hook) vaqiSaM -SA -SI, variSI, valiSaM -SI, matsyaveDanaM -nI. — (Hook for driving an elephant) aNkuSaH -SaM, aNkUzaH -zaM, SfRiH f. — (Bill- hook) dAtraM.
To HOOK , v. a. (Fish) vaqiSena matsyAn vyaD (c. 4. viDyati, vyadDuM) or Df (c. 1. Darati, DarttuM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM), DaraRaM kf, grahaRaM kf.
HOOK-NOSED: SukanAsaH (sA, saM); tuNganAsaH (sA, saM) [not vakranAsaH].
HOOKED (adj.): vakra (f. krA): v. Crooked.
HOOKED , a. (Bent in the form of a hook) vakraH -krA -kraM, aNkuSA- kAraH -rA -raM, aNkuSI -SinI -Si (n), anfjuH -juH -ju, kuYcitaH -tA -taM.
Hoop, s. cakraM, valayaH-yaM. 2 krIqAcakraM. v. t. lohavalayEH yuj 10. 2 uccEH Guz 10.
HOOP (subs.): cakram (= anything circular).
HOOP (v.): (1) citkAraM karoti;(2) uccEH SabdAyate (nomi.).
HOOP , s. (Any thing circular) cakraM, cakravAlaM, valayaH -yaM. — (For playing with) krIqAcakaM, krIQAvalayaH.

To HOOP , v. a. (Bind with hoops) lohavalayAn banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDaM), lohacakrAdiBir yuj (c. 10. yojayati -yituM). — (Shout out) citkAraM kf, citkAraSabdaM kf, uccEHsvareRa udGuz (c. 10. -Gozayati -yituM).
HOOPER , s. (A cooper) lohavalayabanDA m. (nDf), kAzWaBARqakAraH.
HOOPING-COUGH: perh. UrDvaSvAsaH, Bha.
HOOPING-COUGH , s. AkzepakakASaH, hUpSabdapUrvvakaH kASaH, bAlakAnAM kASaH.
HOOPOE: a bird: kAzWakUwaH (?).
Hoot, s. Gu(GU)tkAraH. 2 DikkAraH, uccEH apraSaMsA-sUcanaM, dIrGaGozaH. v. i. GUtkAraravaM kf 8 U, uccEH Araw 1 P or Guz 10, dIrGaM ru 2 P; ‘h(oot) at’ uccEH avajYAM-DikkAraM-sUc 10.
HOOT, HOOTING (subs.): I In gen.: DikkAraH (?) or by circumlo.II Of an owl: GUtkAraH, U.
HOOT (v.): I In gen.: garhayati (garh, c. 10.) (?).II Of an owl: GUtkaroti.

To HOOT , v. n. ru (c. 2. rOti, ravituM), viru, dIrGarutaM kf, dIrGarAvaM kf, GUtkf, GUtkAraM kf, citkAraM kf, uccEHsvareRa udGuz (c. 10. -Gozayati -yituM); ‘to hoot at,’ he, re, are, Dik, hUm, GUt ityAdiSabdEr avamAnaM or avajYAM or aprasAdaM sUc (c. 10. sUcayati -yituM) or ityAdiSabdEr avajYAspadaM kf.
HOOT , HOOTING, s. dIrGarutaM, dIrGarAvaH, rAvaH, GUtkAraH, GUtkftaM, citkAraH, he, re, Dik, GUt ityAdiSabdEr avamAnasUcanaM or aprasAdamUcanaM.

sanskrit.slp1: latAviSezo yasya puzpARi yavarasena saha saMsfjyante
sanskrit.word: लताविशेषो यस्य पुष्पाणि यवरसेन सह संसृज्यन्ते
sanskrit.iast: latāviśeṣo yasya puṣpāṇi yavarasena saha saṃsṛjyante

details.body: Hop, v. i. plu 1 A, valg 1 U, ekapAdena nft 4 P. s. plutaM, valgitaM, plavaH, ekapAdena nftyaM.
HOP (subs.): I A leap: q.v.: ekapAdalamPaH. II A plant: latAviSezaH.
HOP (v.): ekapAdena plavate (plu, c. 1.): v. To leap.
To HOP , v. n. plu (c. 1. plavate, plotuM), valg (c. 1. valgati -lgituM), nft (c. 4. nftyati, narttituM), ekaplAdena plu or valg.
HOP , s. (The plant) latAviSezo yasya puzpARi yavarasena saha saMsfjyante tena ca yavasurA utpadyate. — (Jump) plavaH, plutaM, valgitaM, JampaH, nftyaM, narttanaM, ekapAdena plutaM, valgitaM.

Hope, v. t. ASaMs 1 A, ut-prati-apa-Ikz 1 A, spfh 10, pratyAkAMkz 1 P, vAMC 1 P, ASAM Df or vah 1 P; in implied questions, gen. ex. by api, kaccit or api nAma; ‘I h(ope) this lotus-leaf breeze pleases you’ api suKAyate te nalinIpatra-vAtaH (S. 3); api nAma rAmaBadraH punarapIdaM vanamalaMkuryAt (U. 2), kaccinmfgIRAmanaGA prasUtiH (R. v. 7); ‘I h(ope) not’ na Kalu; na Kalu tAmaBikrudDo guruH (V. 3) ‘I h(ope) the preceptor did not get angry with her’; ‘I scarcely h(op)ed to see you here’ na Kalu me AsIdASaMsA yadatra BavaMtaM prekzizye. s. ASA pratyASA, ASaMsA, AkAMkzA, apekzA, pratIkzA, udIkzaRaM; spfhA, manoraTaH, vAMCa, icCA, ASAbaMDaH. 2 (‘Giving h(ope)’) ASvAsanaM, ASvAsaH; ‘having h(ope)s fulfilled’ pURASa; ‘a vain h(ope)’ vfTABi-lAzaH, moGASA, ‘h(op)ing against h(ope)’ atIva dUrApetaM. [Hope]ful, a. ASAnvita, ASAvat, ASAyukta, ASAbadDa, spfhayAlu, apekzin sapratyASa, ASAvizwa. 2 (Giving hopes) ASAjanana (nI f.), ASAkArin. [Hope]fully, adv. sASaMsaM, sapratyASaM. [Hope]less, a. nirASa, ASAtIta, ASAhIna, hatASa, tyaktASa, nirapekza. [Hope]lessly, adv. nErASyAt, sanarASya.

HOPE (subs.): I Expectation: ASA, prati-, what is not done from h.: ASayA kimiva na kriyate, K.; I have no h. of life: nirASo'smi jIvite, Sa. vi.; the girl entertained h.s of remeeting (her) master: baBuvASAvatI bAlA punarBartfsamAgame, Mah.; false h.: durASA K.: v. Also wish. II That which gives h.:(1) ASA;(2) ASvAsaH, for you are the h. of the distressed: tvaM hyArtAnAM samASvAsaH, Mah.

HOPE (v.): (1) ASAM karoti;(2) ASaMsate (SaMs, c. 1.) (= to apprehend). N.B. In questions, “I h.” may be expr. by the interro. parti- -cles api, kaccit, aTa, we h. the breeze of these lotus-leaves pleases you: api suKAyate te nalinI- patravAtaH, Sa. iii.

HOPE , s. ASA, pratyASA, ASaMsA, AkAMkzA, ASAbanDaH, manoraTaH, apekzA, vyapekzA, pratIkzA, sampratIkzA, spfhA, nirIkzA, udIkzaRaM, IpsitaM, manasvitA; ‘hope of a good issue,’ PalAkAMkzA; ‘having one's hopes fulfilled,’ pUrRamanoraTaH, ASAprAptaH; ‘hopes whose fulfilment is delayed,’ vilambitaPalA manoraTAH; ‘hope-inspiring,’ ASAjananaH -nA -naM.

To HOPE , v. a. and n. ASaMs (c. 1. -SaMsate -situM), AkAMkz (c. 1. -kAMkzati -kzituM), pratyAkAMkz, pratIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), apekz, vyapekz, udIkz, spfh (c. 10. spfhayati -yituM), vAYC (c. 1. vAYCati -YCituM), aBivAYC, ASAM kf, pratyASAM kf, ASaMsAM kf, ASAs (c. 2. SAste -SAsituM); ‘I hardly hoped to see you again,’ na Kalu ma AsId ASaMsA yaTA punarapi tvAM prekzizye; ‘I hope’ may be ex- pressed by the particle kaccit; as, ‘I hope the fever does not pain you much,’ kaccit tvAM nAtibADate jvaraH.
HOPEFUL: I Entertaining hope:(1) ASAvat (f. tI);(2) ASAnvitaH (tA, taM); and sim. comp.s.II Giving hope:(1) ASAjananaH (nI, naM);(2) ASAvarDana (f. nI) (= very h.).

HOPEFUL , a. (Full of hope) ASAvAn -vatI -vat (t), ASAnvitaH -tA -taM, ASAyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, ASAvizwaH -zwA -zwaM, ASAbadDaH -dDA -dDaM, spfhayAluH -luH -lu, AkAMkzI -kziRI -kzi (n), sapratyASaH -SA -SaM, pratyASI -SinI -Si (n), apekzI -kziRI -kzi (n), apekzakaH -kA -kaM. — (Promising, exciting hope) ASAjananaH -nA -naM, ASAkArI -riRI -ri (n).
HOPEFULLY , adv. sapratyASaM, sASaMsaM, ASAMpUrvvaM, ASaMsApUrvvaM.
HOPEFULNESS: (1) ASAvattA;(2) ASAjananatA. For dif. v. Hopeful.
HOPEFULNESS , s. ASAvattvaM, ASAvizwatvaM, sapratyASatvaM.
HOPELESS: I Without hope:(1) nirASaH (SA, SaM);(2) hatASaH (SA, SaM); etc.II Beyond hope: ASAtItaH (tA, taM).
HOPELESS , a. ASAhInaH -nA -naM, nirASaH -SA -SaM, ASArahitaH -tA -taM, gatASaH -SA -SaM, tyaktASaH -SA -SaM, niHpratyASaH -SA -SaM, hatASaH -SA -SaM.
HOPELESSLY , adv. nirASaM, niHpratyASaM, ASAM vinA, gatASaM.
HOPELESSNESS: (1) nErASyam;(2) nirASatA;(3) hatASatA; etc.
HOPELESSNESS , s. nErASyaM, nirASatA, ASAhInatA, ASArAhityaM.
HOPPER: in a mill: SasyADAraH, Williams.
HOPPER , s. (One who hops) ekapAdena plutakArI m. (n), ekapAdena narttakaH. — (In a mill) SasyADAraH, SasyapAtraM.
HOPPING , s. ekapAdena narttanaM or nftyaM or plutakaraRaM or valgitakaraRaM.
Hora, s. muhurtaH, GawikA. [Hor]al, [Hor]ary, a. mOhUrtika (kI f.).
HORAL , HORARY, a. mOhUrttikaH -kI -kaM, GawikAvizayaH -yA -yaM.
Horde, s. mahAn gaRaH, bfhatsaMGaH, mahOGaH, stomaH; See Multitude.
HORDE: saNGaH (= crowd, flock: q.v.).
HORDE , s. asTiravAsinAM or paryyawanakAriRAM mlecCapuruzARAM samUhaH or saNGaH or vfhatkulaM or vfhadgaRaH, SavaragaRaH, kirAtagaRaH.

Horizon, s. kzitijaM, diNmaMqalaM, dikcakraM, aMbarAMtaH; cakraM, maMqalaM; ‘the eastern h(orizon)’ prAcI-EMdrI-dik, prAcImUlam. Horizontal, a. sama, digaMtasama, anuprasTa; ‘h(orizontal) plane’ samaBUBAgaH, samA BUmiH. [Horizontal]ly, adv. samaM, anuprasTaM.

HORIZON: (1) harijam, as a sign comes to the h.: yadvadrASirvrajati harijam, Ja. v. 17.;(2) kzitijam, that point is then on the h.: tallagnaM kzitije tadA, Su. iii. 48. N.B. Colloquially diNmaRqalaH and sim. comp.s. would do.
HORIZON , s. diNmaRqalaM, maRqalaM, cakravAlaM, cakraM, digantaH, AkASakakzA, ambarAntaM -ntaH, cakrapAlaH. ‘The eastern horizon,’ prAcI dika, prAcImalaM.
HORIZON , s. kzitijaM, kujaM; ‘sensible or visible horizon,’ dfzwi- maryyAdA, cakravAlaM; ‘glow of the horizon,’ digbAhaH.
HORIZONTAL: samaH (mA, maM) (= level: q.v.).

HORIZONTAL , a. anuprasTaH -sTA -sTaM, anvAyatanaH -nA -na, digantasamaH -mA -maM, samaH -mA -maM, samareKaH -KA -KaM, sama -yaH -sTA -sTaM, sapAwaH -wA. -waM; ‘a horizontal line,’ dvijyAmArgaM, samareKA; ‘plane,’ samAnaBUBAgaH.
HORIZONTAL , a. kzitijEkasUtraH -trA -traM, kzitijasamasUtraH &c.
HORIZONTALLY: perh. samaBUmO (= on a level).
HORIZONTALLY , adv. anuprasTaM, anvAyatanaM, samaM, samareKaM, samAnarUpeRa.

Horn, s. SfMgaM, vizARaH-RaM, kURikA; ‘h(orn) of a buffalo’ gavalaM. 2 kAhalaH-lA, SaMKaH. 3 caMdrAgraM, caMdraSiKA. [Horn]ed, a. SfMgin, vizA-Rin, SfMgayukta-viSizwa. 2 SfMgAkAra, SfMgA-kfti. [Horn]y, a. SAMrga (rgI f.). 2 kaWina; See Hard.

HORN: I Lit.:(1) SfNgam, the root of a h.: SfNga- mUlam; the tip of a h.: SfNgAgram, Pa.; sharp-h. ed: tIkzRaSfNgaH, Ram.;(2) vizARam, struck with h. s.: vizARErAhataH (tA, taM), M.n.II A wind-instru- -ment: kAhalA, blew h.s: kAhalAH pUrayAYcakruH, B. xiv. 3.

HORN , s. (Of an animal) SfNgaM, vizARaH -RI -RaM, kURikA, kAhalaH -lA -likA; ‘of a buffalo,’ gavalaM. — (Wind-instrument) SaNKaH, kAhalaH -lA; ‘to blow a horn,’ SaNKaM DmA (c. 1. Damati, DmAtuM) or praDmA. — (Of the moon) candraSiKA, candraSfNgaM, vandrAgraM.
HORN-BOOK , s. bAlakasya AramBapustakaM or AdipustakaM or praTamapAWagranTaH.
HORN-OWL , s. ulUkaBedaH, SfNgiRapecakaH, SfNgikOSikaH.

sanskrit.slp1: nftyaviSezaH yasmin narttako hastapAdAdi itastataH kzipraM
sanskrit.word: नृत्यविशेषः यस्मिन् नर्त्तको हस्तपादादि इतस्ततः क्षिप्रं
sanskrit.iast: nṛtyaviśeṣaḥ yasmin narttako hastapādādi itastataḥ kṣipraṃ

details.body: HORN-PIPE , s. nftyaviSezaH yasmin narttako hastapAdAdi itastataH kzipraM saYcAlayati, nAvikanftyaM.
HORNBILL: perh. KawvANgaH, “KawvANgAn lubDakAMstaTA”, Mat.
HORNBOOK: praTamapAWaH (?): v. Primer, hand- -book.
HORNED: SfNgin (f. RI). H. moon: sinIvAlI.
HORNED , a. SfNgI -NgiRI -Ngi (n), SfNgiRaH -RA -RaM, vizARI -RinI -Ri (n), SfNgaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM; ‘in the form of a horn,’ SfNgA- kAraH -rA -raM; ‘horned moon,’ sinIvAlI.
Hornet, s. varawA, bfhadgaMqolaH.
HORNET: (1) varawA;(2) vizaSfNgin (m.) or viza- SUkaH (?).
HORNET , s. vfhadvaralaBedaH, vfhadBfNgarolaH, vizaSfNgI m. (n), vizaSUkaH

SatrUyati), dviz (c. 2. dvezwi -zwuM), vidviz, paryyavasTA (c. 1. -tizWati -sTAtuM).

Hot, a. uzRa, AtapAkrAMta, Atapavat, taptaM, saM-ut-tapta, sozRa; praKara, ugra, tigma, caMqa, Kara, tIvra, tIkzRa. 2 grIzma, nEdAGa (GI f.), Garma in comp. 3 SIGra-sulaBa-kopin, kroDin, saMraMBin. 4 sAhasin, tIkzRakarman; ‘h(ot) weather or season’ grIzmaH, nidAGaH, Garma-grIzma-uzRa-kAlaH; ‘to make h(ot)’ tap c.; ‘to be h(ot)’ tap 1 P, 4 A, uzRIBU; ‘h(ot)-bed’ uzRa-sTalaM, (fig.) kzetraM; ‘h(ot)-blooded’ or ‘h(ot)-headed’ caMqaprakfti-SIla, saMraMBin, SIGra-kopin, uttapta, uccaMqa, tIkzRakarman, sAhAsi-ka, sAhasin. [Hot]ness, s. uzRatA, tApaH, praKaratA, ugratA, caMqatA, tigmatA, OzmyaM, nidAGaH, GarmatA. 2 uttApaH, tIkzRatA, saMraMBaH, vyagratA; ‘h(otness) of temper’ SIGrakopitvaM, caMqatA.

HOT: I Lit.:(1) tapta (f. ptA), saM-, pra-, aBi-, upa-, h. iron: ayo'Bitaptam, R.; h. water: taptaM vAri, V.;(2) uzRa (f. zRA). h. and acrid: uzRakawukaH (kA, kaM), Sa.; slightly h.: kavozRa (f. zRA);(3) Garma (f. rmA) (rare), h.-rayed (the sun): Garma- dIDitiH;(4) grIzma (f. zmA) (rare);(5) jvalat (f. ntI) (= burning of h. and glowing heat). Ph.: h. season:(1) grIzmaH;(2) nidADaH;(3) GarmaH, R.;(4) tapaH, Si.;(5) uzRaH, A.;(6) SuciH, Ri.:(7) grIzmakAlaH, nidAGakAlaH, and sim. comp.s.II To the taste (tIkzRa) (f. kzRA), pepper is acrid and h.: maricaM kawukaM tIkzRam, Bha.: v. Sharp. N.B. Not uzRa or Darma which is = heating, exciting heat.III Fig., vehement, furious:(1) ugra (f. grA);(2) caRqa (f. RqA,), pra-.

HOTLY: (1) caRqam, pra-, ut-;(2) ugram.

HOUSE (subs.): I Lit.:(1) gfham (best equiv.: gfhAH in pl.=h. with its surroundings or inmates), to the h. of the chief of Vidarbha: gfhAn vidarBADipateH, N. xvi. 1.; where h. s shone as if with edges of thatches: gfhARi niDrEriva yatra rejuH, Si. iii. 49.;(2) geham, she is fortune in h. iyaM gehe lakzmIH, U. i. 38.; the mistress of my h.: madragehinI, Me. ii. 16.;(3) A(a)garam, our h.: asmadIyAgAram, Ma.;(4) kulam (rare), h. of god: devakulam, Mr. ii.; (5) SaraRam (rare: prop=protection), h. of fire: agniSaraRam, Sa. iv.;(6) Bavanam (= building): v. Edifice;(7) niketanam (= abode: q.v.);(8) Ayatanam: v. Temple.II Family, race: q.v.: gfham, is this becoming your h.: yuktametadvo gfhasya, Vi. iv.III A firm: gfham (after Bengali).IV In chess: gfham.V A legislative body: samA, “to bring down the whole h.”: samagrasaBAgfham (or SrAvakAn) Avarjayati (?).

Hover, v. i. paritaH visfp 1 P or qI 1 A, AkASe vyAvft 1 A or visfp or vical 1 P, pariBram 1, 4 P; ‘h(over) about’ maMqale car 1 P, dIpasyopari maMqale carati (Mr. 3); maMqalAkAreRa Bram. 2 (fig.) viSaMk 1 A, vikxp 1 A, vicar c. [Hover]ing, s. pariBramaRaM; maMqalAvftti f.
HOVER: I Lit.: perh. pariqIyate (qI, c. 4.). II Fig., to hang about: parito visarpati (sfp, c. 1.) (?); paryavekzate (Ikz, c. 1.) (= to look about).

To HOVER , v. n. vihAyasA or vyomamaDye vft (c. 1. varttate -rttituM) or vyAvft, AkASamaDye mastakopari vft, praqInam akftvA UrdDvaviyati visfp (c. 1. -sarpati -sraptu) or vical (c. 1. -calati -lituM), vyomamaDye pakzAsPAlanaM kftvA niScalo vft. — (Hesitate, waver) vilamb (c. 1. -lambate -mbituM), dola (nom. dolAyate), Andola (nom. Andolayati -yituM), vikxp (c. 1. -kalpate -lpituM), vicar (c. 10. -cArayati -yituM), viSaNk (c. 1. -hlaNkate -NkituM).

How, adv. kaTaM, kena prakAreRa-rUpeRa. 2 kiyat (in ‘how long’, ‘how far’); ‘h(ow) much’ kiyat; ‘h(ow) many’ kati (pl.); ‘h(ow) long’ kiyacciraM, kiyaMtaM kAlaM; ‘h(ow) many kinds’ kativiDAH; ‘h(ow) many times’ katikftvaH; ‘h(ow) now’ nanu, nanu BoH; ‘h(ow) far’ kiyaddUraM, kiyadavaDi; ‘h(ow) much more, -less’ kimuta, kiM punaH, kimu; ‘h(ow) else’ aTa kiM; with adj. ex. by aho; ‘h(ow) pleasing’ aho maDuraM; aho pApaM, &c.

HOW (adv.): I In what way:(1) kaTam, h. can a servant be without fault: kaTaM nu dAso niraparADaH, V.; h. (you) fell into the hands of the Chandal: kaTaM caRqAlahastagamanam, K.;(2) kena prakAreRa, teach me h. to make prostration: kena prakAreRa daRqapraRAmaH kartavyastanmAM Sikzaya, V.t. N.B.(1) In the last sense, h. is often not expr., you know (h.) to make (one) take: jAnAsi grAhayitum, K.;(2) sometimes expr. by kim (= what), h. is (= what has happened to) Sāgarikā: sAgarikAyAH kiM vartate, Ra. iv.II To what degree: kiyat. N.B. For h. many, h. long, etc.: v. Many, long, etc.

HOW , adv. kaTaM, kiM, kena prakAreRa, kena rUpeRa, kinnu, kutas, kimuta; ‘how much, how many, how little, how long, &c.,’ kiyAn -yatI -yat (t) or kiyat indec., katiH -tiH -ti or kati in comp.; as, ‘how long?’ kiyatkAlaM, kiyantaM kAlaM, kiyatA kAlena, kati- kAlaM; ‘how long!’ kiyacciraM; ‘how many sorts?’ kativiDaH -DA -DaM; ‘how many times?’ katikftvas; ‘for how much?’ kiyatA mUlyena; ‘how far?’ kiyatparyyantaM, kimparyyantaM, kiyadavaDi; ‘how much more,’ kimpunar, kimuta, kimu, kim, kutaHpunar; how much less,’ kimuta, kimu; ‘how so?’ kimiti, kimiva; how else,’ aTakim; ‘how wonderful,’ kimAScaryyaM; ‘how do you do?’ kiM kzemam asti BavataH, kiM kuSalam asti BavataH, kIdfSI sTitir BavataH; ‘how are we to act?’ kim asmABiH karaRIyaM; ‘he knows not how to act,’ yaTAkAryyaM na jAnAti; ‘how great is that darkness!’ so'nDakAraH kiyAn mahAn; ‘any how,’ yaTAkaTaYcit, yaTAtaTA, kaTaYcana, kaTaYcit.
HOWBEIT: taTApi.: v. Nevertheless, yet.
HOWBEIT , adv. taTApi, taTEva, taTAca, kiYca, api, apitu, kintu.
Howdah, s. varaMqakaH.
HOWDAH: varaRqaH, -kaH, Wilson.
HOWDAH , s. (On the back of an elephant) varaRqakaH.

However, Howsoever, adv. yaTAtaTA, yenakena prakAreRa; (with adj.) by api, or by nAma with imp. of verb; ‘h(owsoever) industrious a man may be’ dIrGavyavasAyopi naraH, karotu nAma vyavasAyaM naraH (H. 2). conj. (Howbeit) kiMtu, api tu, tu, paraMtu, taTApi, punaH.

HOWEVER (adv.): I In whatever way:(1) yaTA yaTA;(2) yena yena prakAreRaII To whatever degree: expr. by super. and api, h. poor: atyantadaridro'pi (f. drApi); h. learned: paRqita- varizWo'pi; h. often: yAvato yAvato vArAn.III At least: antataH.
HOWEVER (conj.): (1) parantu: v. But.;(2) taTApiH v. Yet.
HOWEVER , adv. taTApi, kiYca, apitu, kintu, tu, parantu, punar; ‘in whatever manner,’ yatprakAreRa.
HOWITZER , s. antaragnivalena lohagulikAprakzepakaM yudDayantraM.

Howl, v. i. AkraMd 1 P, utkruS 1 P, uccEH ras-raw 1 P, garj 1 P, dIrGaM vi-ru 2 P, rE 1 P. [Howl]ing, s. utkroSaH-SanaM, AkraM-danaM, dIrGarutaM, ArawanaM, ra(rA)vaH, dIrGaravaH, garjanaM, rasitaM; ‘h(owling) of dogs’ BazaRaM, bukkanaM, rAyaRaM.
HOWL (subs.): (1) cI(ci)tkftam;(2) Akranditam; (3) cItkAraH.
HOWL (v.): (1) cI(ci)tkAraM karoti;(2) Akrandati (krand, c. 1.).

To HOWL , v. n. ru (c. 2. rOti, ravituM), viru, dIrGarAvaM kf, dIrGarutaM kf, garj (c. 1. garjati -rjituM), Baz (c. 1. Bazati -zituM), rE (c. 1. rAyati rAtuM), ras (c. 1. rasati -situM), raw (c. 1. rawati -wituM), vAS (c. 1. vASate -SituM).
HOWL , HOWLING, s. rAvaH, rutaM, dIrDarAvaM, dIGarutaM, garjanaM, rAyaRaM, BAzaH, BazaRaM, bukkanaM, vASitaM, muKaGaRwA; ‘making a howling,’ dIrGarAvaH -vI -vaM.
HOWLING (adj.): “h. wilderness”: nirmAnuzamaraRyam.
HOWSOEVER , adv. yatprakAreRa, yena prakAreRa, yaTA yaTA, yaTAtaTA, taTApi
To HOX , v. a. jaNGAsTiSirAM Cid (c. 7. Cinatti, CettuM).
HOY: potaH: v. Ship.
HOY , s. vfhannOkAviSezaH, viSAlanOkA.
HOYDEN: grAmya (f. myA): v. Rude.
Hub, s. nABi f. 2 tsaruH. 3 lakzyaM, SaravyaM.
HUBBLE-BUBBLE: gurguriH (in Bengali).
Hubbub, s. kolAhalaH, kalakalaH; tumulaM, tumularavaH-nAdaH, saMkIrRanAdaH.
HUBBUB , s. kolAhalaH, kalakalaH, kalaravaH, rAsaH, halahalASabdaH, kAla- kIlaH, tumulaM, viplavaH, kalahaH.
HUBBUS: kolAhalaH: v. Tumult, uproar.
HUCKABACK , s. nAnAreKANkitaH kzOmapawaviSezaH.
HUCKLEBACKED , a. nyubjaH -bjA -bjaM, kubjaH -bjA -bjaM, vakrakanDaraH -rA -raM
Hucklebone, s. SroRyasTi n.
HUCKLEBONE , s. kawyasTi n., kawAsTi n., SroRyasTi n., jaGanAsTi.
Huckster, s. kzudrapaRyavikrayin-vikretf m. v. i. kzudrapaRyAni vi-krI 9 A.
HUCKSTER (subs.): kzudrapaRyavikrayikaH, -vikretf (m.) etc.
HUCKSTER (v.): kzudrapaRyAni vikrIRIte (krI, c. 9.).
HUCKSTER , s. kzudrabARijyakArI m. (n), tucCabARijyakft, kutsitaba- Rik m. (j).
To HUCKSTER , v. n. tucCabARijyaM kf, tucCaprakAreRa or nIcaprakAreRa or kutsitaprakAreRa bARijyaM kf.

Huddle, v. t. piMqIkf 8 U, saM-kF 6 P, saMmiSr 10, saMkulIkf, saMpiMqayati (D.). 2 saMkzuB c.; sasaMBramaM vi-DA 3 U or kf. v. i. saMkulIBU 1 P, saMmiSrI-saMkarI-BU, saMkF pass., piMqIBU. s. saMkulaM, saMkaraH, saMkzoBaH, saMkIrRatA.
HUDDLE (subs.): janasaMmardaH (of person); saNkaraH (of thing).

To HUDDLE , v. a. sammiSrIkf, astavyastIkf, saNkulIkf, saNkarIkf, sammiSr (c. 10. -miSrayati -yituM), sambAD (c. 1. -bADate -DituM), aDarottarIkf, saMkzuB.
To HUDDLE , v. n. sammiSrIBU, saNkulIBU, saNkIrRIBU, saNkarIBU, astavyastIBU, aDarottarIBU, sambADIBU.
HUDDLE , s. astavyastatA -tvaM, aDarottaraM, saNkaraH, sANkaryyaM, saNkzoBaH.

details.body: Hue, s. rAgaH, raMgaH, varRaH, CAyA, Cavi f. 2 AkroSaH; ‘h(ue) and cry’ kalakalaH, kolA-halaH, janaravaH, saMhUti f.

HUE (subs.): I Colour: q.v.: raNgaH.II A shouting, so when a h. and cry is raised after a thief, those who hear and do not run after him also share in his guilt: utkroSatAM janAnAntu hriyamARe Dane taTA . SrutvA ye nABiDAvanti te'pi taddozaBAginaH.., N.s.
HUE , s. (Dye, colour) varRaH, rAgaH, raNgaH, CAyA, CaviH f. — (Hue and cry) janaravaH. bahuBiH kftA saMhUtiH, janaGozaRA

Huff, v. t. vistF c., Svi c., vfD c. 2 sadarpaM nirBarts or tarj 10 A. v. i. Svi 1 P, sPAy 1 A, vfD 1 A. 2 dfp 4 P, vikatT 1 A, pragalB 1 A. s. kopaH, rozaH, saMraMBaH; See Anger. 2 darpaH, OdDatyaM, nirBartsanaM. 3 udDataH, darpADmAtaH, dAMBikaH, vikatTanaH. HUFF (subs.): I Rage: q.v.: manyuH.II A boaster: utsiktaH.

HUFFER , s. dAmBikaH, BartsanakAraH, vikatTI m. (n), DarpI m. (n), SUrammanyaH.

HUFFISH , a. (Angry) kroDAvizwaH -zwA -zwaM, kopI -pinI -pi (n), saropaH -pA -paM, sakopaH -pA -paM. — (Arrogant) dfptaH -ptA -ptaM, garvvI -rvviRI -rvvi (n), udDataH -tA -taM, DarpI -rpiRI -rpi (n), AtmaSlAGI -GinI -Gi (n).

HUG (v.): parizvajate (svaYj, c. 1.): v. To embrace.

HUG , s. AliNganaM -NgitaM, ASlezaH, parizvaNgaH, bAhUpapIqaH, aNkapAlI.

Huge, a. mahat, bfhat, sTUla, viSAla, vipula, guru, bfhatparimARa, atimahat-bfhat-. 2 (In body) sTUla-kAya-deha, bfhacCarIra, mahA-kAya, vipulAMga (gI f.). [Huge]ly, adv. ati-mahat, atyaMtaM, atimAtraM. [Huge]ness, s. ati-bfhattvaM, sTUlatA, viSAlatA.
HUGE: (1) viSAlaH (lA, laM);(2) vipulaH (lA, laM); (3) mahApramARa (f. RA): v. Large, immense.

HUGE , a. vfhan -hatI -hat (t), ativfhan &c., suvfhan &c., mahAn -hatI -hat (t), atimahAn &c., sumahAn &c., sTUlaH -lA -laM, ativiSAlaH -lA -laM, vfhatparimARaH -RA -RaM, aparimitaH -tA -taM, varIyAn -yasI -yaH (s), varizWaH -zWA -zWa, garizWaH -zWA -zWaM. — (In body) mahAkAyaH -yA -yaM, atikAyaH -yA -yaM, vfhatkAyaH -yA -yaM, vfhacCarIraH -rA -raM.
HUGELY: (1) viSAlam;(2) vipulam: v. Largely.
HUGELY , adv. sumahat, atimahat, suvfhat, atyantaM, atimAtraM, aparimitaM.
HUGENESS: (1) viSAlatA;(2) vipulatA: v. Large- -ness.
HUGENESS , s. muvfhattvaM, vfhattvaM, mahattvaM, sumahattvaM, atimahattvaM, sTUlatA, ati- viSAlatA, aparimitatvaM, suvipulatA, kAyavfhattvaM, vfhatkAyatvaM.
HUGGED , p. p. AliNgitaH -tA -taM, ASlizwaH -zwA -zwaM, pIqitaH -tA -taM.
HUGGER-MUGGER , s. rahas n., gUQatA, pracCannatA; ‘in huggermuggerhugger-mugger,’ rahasi, rahasyaM, niBftaM, pracCannaM, guptaM, upAMSu.
Hulk, s. jIrRanOkA.

HULK , s. jIrRanOkA, guRakUpakAdirahitA nOkA, rajjukUpakAdihIno nOkAyAH sTUlaBAgaH
Hull, s. (potasya) sTUlaBAgaH. 2 puwaH-waM, koSaH-zaH, tvac f., AvezwanaM, tuzaH (of grain).
HULL: I Of fruits: puwaH.II Of grain: tuzaH. III Of a ship: expr. by potaH or nOH or nOkA.
HULL , s. (Integument) kaYcukaH, AvezwanaM, parivezwanaM, koSaH, kozaH, puwaH, tvak f. (c) — (Of a ship) guRakUpakAdiBinno nOkABAgaH, nOkAyAH sTUlaBAgaH or kAyaH.
HULLY , a. koSavAn -vatI -vat (t), tuzavAn &c., tvagyuktaH -ktA -ktaM

Hum, v. i. guMj 1 P, vi-, ru 2 P, huMkf 8 U, aspazwaM nisvan 1 P or Dvan 1 P. [Hum]ming, s. guMjanaM, guMjitaM, kalaravaH-svaraH, vi-, rutaM-rAvaH, JaMkAraH, huMkAraH, huMkftaM, aspazwa-DvaniH-nisvanaH-nAdaH, kalakalaH.
HUM (subs.): I Buzz: q.v.: huNkf tam, with the h. of bees: maDulihAM huNkf tena, K.II Of men: kalakalaH.III A low murmur: huNkAraH, Sa.
HUM (v.): (1) huNkaroti;(2) guYjati (juYja, c. 1.) (= to buzz).
HUM (interj.): hum, huM rAkzasaH, Vi. i.
To HUM , v. n. guYj (c. 1. guYjati -YjituM), ru (c. 2. rOti, ravituM), viru, raRaraRaM kf; ‘to hum and haw,’ BinnasvareRa or sKalitavAcA vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM).
HUM ! interj hum, hUm, A, As, hA, aho, ahovat, tAvat, kiM.
HUM , s. (Buzzing sound) kalaH, kalaravaH, kalakalaH, kalasvaraH, rutaM, virutaM, rAvaH, virAvaH, guYjanaM, guYjitaM, marmaraH, JaNkAraH, raRatkAraH; ‘of bees,’ alivirAvaH, alivirutaM.
HUM-DRUM , a. mandaH -ndA -ndaM, virasaH -sA -saM, arasikaH -kA -kaM, PalguH -lguH -lgu, kazwakaraH -rA -raM, jaqaH -qA -qaM.

Human, a. mAnuza (zI f.), pOruzeya (yI f.), manuzyajAtIya, mAnavIya-na; gen. ex. by manuzya or nara in comp.; ‘in h(uman) accents’ manuzyavAcA; ‘uttered h(uman) accents’ mAnuzIM giramudIrayAmAsa; ‘h(uman) nature’ mAnuzyakaM, puruzatvaM, narasvaBAvaH; ‘h(uman)-form’ mAnuzI tanuH, nararUpaM; ‘a h(uman) brute’ narapaSuH; ‘h(uman) kind’ manuzya-nf-jAti f. manuzyavargaH. [Human]ize, v. t. vi-nI 1 P, SizwAcAraM-saByarItiM Sikz c. or SAs 2 P. [Human]ly, adv. naravat, mAnuzaprakAreRa. Humane, a. dayAlu, kfpAlu, sadaya, parahitakAma, paropakAraSIla, anukaMpin, karuRA-dayA-SIla, dayAvat, karu-RArdra, dayArdra, parahitEzin, Apanna-dIna-anu-kaMpin; See Kind. [Human]ity, s. dayA, karuRA, kfpA, dayAlutA, ApannAnukaMpA, dInavAtsalyaM, dayASIlatA, parahitecCA. 2 mAnuzyaM-zyakaM, manuzyatA, mAnuzatA, mAnavatvaM. 3 manuzyAH, manuzyavargaH-jAtiH. [Humane]ly, adv. sadayaM, sakaruRaM, parahitecCayA, sAnukaMpaM.

HUMAN: (1) by comp., in h. tongue: manuzyavAcA, R.; h. nature: mAnuzatA, K.: v. Man;(2) mAnuzaH (zI, zaM), h. body: mAnuzI tanuH, R. xvi. 22.; (3) mAnavaH (vI, vaM) or- vIyaH (yA, yaM), h. form: mAnavaM rUpam, M. n.

HUMAN , a. mAnuzaH -zI -zaM -zikaH -kI -kaM, mAnavInaH -nA -naM, mAnavIyaH -yA -yaM, pOruzaH -zI -zaM, pOruzeyaH -yI -yaM, janakIyaH -yA -yaM, nAraH -rI -raM, manuzyajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, lOkikaH -kI -kaM; ‘human na- ture,’ puruzatvaM -tA, manuzyatvaM -tA, mAnuzyaM, mAnuzatvaM; ‘human race,’ manuzyajAtiH f., manuzyavargaH, nfjAtiH f.; ‘human form,’ nararUpaM; ‘human art,’ manuzyakalA; ‘a human brute,’ puruzapaSuH m.
HUMANE: dayAlu (mfn.): v. Kind, benevolent.

HUMANELY: sadayam: v. Kindly.
HUMANELY , adv. sakaruRaM, sakAruRyaM, sAnukampaM, sadayaM, dayASIlatvAt, suSIlavat, parahitecCayA.
HUMANIST , s. SAstrajYaH, SAstravyutpannaH, SabdaSAstravid m., vidvajjanaH.
HUMANITY: I Human nature:(1) manuzyatA, -tvam;(2) mAnuzyam.II Mankind: q.v.: manuzyAH (m. pl.).III Humane feeling: dayA: v. Kindness.

HUMANITY , s. (Benevolence, compassion) dayA, dayASIlatA, dayAlutA, kAruRyaM, karuRA, karuRASIlatvaM, anukampA, kfpA, parahitecCA, paropa- kAraSIlatA, hitakAmyA, upakAraparatA, karuRArdratA, sAnukampatA, Apa- nnarakzaRaM. — (Nature of man) puruzatA -tvaM, mAnuzatA, manuzyatA -tvaM, mAnuzyaM, mAnavatvaM, mAnavyaM.
HUMANIZE: vinayati (ni, c. 1.): v. To civilize.
To HUMANIZE , v. a. SizwAcArAn or AryyavyavahArAn Sikz (c. 10. Sikza- yati -yituM) or SAs (c. 2. SAsti, SAsituM), SizwIkf, suSIlIkf, vinItaM -tAM -taM kf, saByaM -ByAM -ByaM kf.
HUMANKIND , s. manuzyajAtiH f., nfjAtiH f., manuzyavargaH, puruzavargaH.
HUMANLY: manuzyavat, “H. speaking”: manuzyabudDpA.

HUNGRY, HUNGERED: (1) kzuDitaH (tA, taM), I am h., my life is going out: kzuDito'haM gataprARaH, Mah.; (2) bumukzitaH (tA, taM), the h. monkey: buBukzitaH kapiH, A.r.;(3) kzuDArta (f. rtA), kzuDAvizwa (f. zwA), kzuDApIqitaH (tA, taM), etc.; you are h.: kzuDalurBavAn, P. i. 16.

HUNGRY , a. kzuDArttaH -rttA -rttaM, kzuDitaH -tA -taM, kzutpIqitaH -tA -taM, kzuDA- pIqitaH -tA -taM, kzuDAturaH -rA -raM, buBukzitaH -tA -taM, buBukzuH -kzuH -kzu, jiGatsuH -tsuH -tsu, AhArArTI -rTinI -rTi (n), annArTI &c., annalipsuH -psuH -psu, AhAralipsuH -psuH -psu, aSanAyitaH -tA -taM, kzuDAvyAkulaH -lA -laM; ‘hungry and thirsty,’ kzutpipAsitaH -tA -taM, kzuttfzRopa- pIqitaH -tA -taM. — (Lean) kfSaH -SA -SaM, apuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, vipuzwaH -zwA -zwaM.
HUNGRY , a. dagDodaraH -rA -raM, kzuDAnalavidagDaH -gDA -gDaM.
HUNKS , s. kfpaRaH, kadaryyaH, DanaloBI m. (n), mitampacaH.

Hunt, v. mfg 10 A, mfgayAM kf 8 U, (mfgayA-yAM) anuDAv 1 P, anusf 1 P, anuvft 1 A, anubaMD 9 P. 2 anviz 4 P, nirUp 10. [Hunt]ing, s. mfgayA, AKewaH, mfgavyaM, AcCodanaM, pApardDi f. 2 anusaraRaM, anvezaRaM, mArgaRaM, anuDAvanaM; lABecCA, lipsA; ‘h(unting)-dress’ mfgayAvezaH; ‘h(unting)-dog’ viSvakadruH, mfgayAku-kkuraH. [Hunt]er, Huntsman, s. vyADaH, lubDakaH, mfgayuH, AKewakaH, mfgavaDAjIvaH; jIvAMtakaH; SAkunikaH (of birds); vAgurikaH, jAlikaH (with nets).

HUNT (v. t.): I Lit.: mfgayate (mfg, c. 10.) or mfgayAM karoti or carati (car, c. 1.), Ram.II Fig.: mfgayate, a gem does not seek, but it is h. ed: na ratnamanvizyati mfgyate hi tat, Sa.: v. To search.

HUNT, HUNTING (subs.): (1) mfgayA, there is nothing so beneficial as h. yaTA mfgayA hyOpakArikI na taTAnyat, D. viii.; to go out (for) h.: mfgayAM yAti, Mah.; devoted to h.: mfgayASIlaH (lA, laM), Sa. ii.;(2) AKewaH, -kaH, deer. h.: hariRAKewkaH, K. s. ix. 74.;(3) mfgavyam (rare), h.-forest: mfgavyasatram, Ki. xiii. 9.

To HUNT , v. a. and n. (Chase) mfg (c. 10. mfgayate -yituM), mfgayAM kf, AKiw (c. 1. -Kewati -wituM), parikal (c. 10. -kAlayati -yituM). — (Pursue, follow after, search for) anusf (c. 1. -sarati -sarttuM), anuDAv (c. 1. -DAvati -vituM), paScAdDAv, anuvft (c. 1. -varttate -rttituM), paScAdvft, anviz (c. 4. -izyati -ezituM).
HUNT , s. (Chase) mfgayA, mfgavyaM, KewaH -waM, AKewaH, AkzodanaM, AcCodanaM, pApardDiH f., parADiH f. — (Pursuit, search) anusaraRaM, anuDAvanaM, anvezaRaM -RA -paryyezaRA, mfgaRaM, mArgaRaM.
HUNTED , p. p. mfgitaH -tA -taM, anusftaH -tA -taM, anuDAvitaH -tA -taM, AKe- witaH -tA -taM, anvizwaH -zwA -zwaM, anvezitaH -tA -taM.
HUNTER: I One who hunts:(1) vyADaH (= professional h.);(2) mfgayuH (rare:) of more gen. application).II A hunting horse: vAjin (m.), R. ix. 56. (?): v. Horse. III A hound: mfgayAkukkuraH; AKewikaH.

HUNTER , s. (One who pursues wild animals) vyADaH, mfgayuH m., lubDakaH, mfgabaDAjIvaH, mfgajIvanaH, AKewakaH, mfgAdipaSuhantA m. (ntf), sOkarikaH, anDraH, KawwikaH; ‘with nets,’ jAlikaH. — (Horse) mfgayASvaH.

HUNTING , s. mfgayA, mfgavyaM, KewaH -waM, AKewaH, AkzodanaM, AcCodanaM, pApardDiH f., parADiH f.; ‘hunting-knife,’ karttarikA; ‘hunting- dog,’ AKewakaH SvA m. (n), mfgayAkukkuraH; ‘hunting appoint- ments,’ mfgayAveSaH. — (Pursuit, search) anusaraRaM, anuDAvanaM, anve- [Page354-b+ 51] zaRaM -RA, paryyezaRA, mfgaRaM, mArgaRaM.
HUNTING-BOX, HUNTING-SEAT: mfgayAsTalI.
HUNTING-HORN , s. mfgayASaNKaH, mfgavyaSaNKaH, vyADavAditaM SfNgaM or vizARaM.
HUNTRESS , s. vyADI f., vyADastrI, AKewakI, mfgayAkAriRI.
HUNTSMAN: I A hunter: q.v.II A servant: mfgayApuruzaH (?).
HUNTSMAN , s. mfgayAkArI m. (n), mfgavyakArI m., mfgayuH m., AKewakaH.
HUNTSMANSHIP , s. mfgayAvidyA, mfgavyavidyA, AKewavidyA.
Hurdle, s. kAzWAvaraRaM.
HURDLE: *kAzWabanDaH or kAzWaroGaH.
HURDLE , s. kAzWaSalAkAnirmmitam avaroDakaM or AvaraRaM, stamBakaraH.
HURDY-GURDY , s. karkaSaSabdaH satantrIvAdyaviSezaH.

Hurl, v. t. (tarasA-savegaM) kzip 6 P, vi-sfj-muc 6 P, prAs 4 U, Ir c., prez c., prahf 1 P; ‘h(url) down’ ni ava-pat c., avaBraMS c., aDaH-kzip. s. kzepaH-paRaM, pAtanaM. 2 tumulaM, kolA-halaH. [Hurl]ing, s. kzepaRaM; ‘h(urling) of stones’ SilAvarzaH-AsAraH.
HURL (v.): (1) kzipati (kzip, c. 6.): v. To cast, throw;(2) pAtayati (c. of pat) (= to cause to fall).
HURL (subs.): I A cast: q.v.: kzepaH.II Tumult: q.v.: tumulam.

To HURL , v. a. kzip (c. 6. kzipati, kzeptuM), prakzip, as (c. 4. asyati, asituM), prAs, Ir (c. 10. Irayati, -yituM), udIr, samIr, muc (c. 6. muYcati, moktuM), pramuc, sfj (c. 6. sfjati, srazwuM), vyavasfj, pat (c. 10. pAta- yati -yituM), prahf (c. 1. -harati -te -harttuM), prez (c. 10. prezayati -yituM, rt. iz), udgur (c. 6. -gurate -rituM); ‘to hurl stones,’ SilApraharaRaM kf; ‘is hurled down,’ nipAtyate.
HURL , s. (Throw) kzepaH -paRaM, asanaM, pAtanaM. — (Tumult) tumulaM, ko- lAhalaH, viplavaH, qimbaH.
HURLED , p. p. kziptaH -ptA -ptaM, prakziptaH -ptA -ptaM, astaH -stA -staM, prAstaH -stA -staM, pAtitaH -tA -taM, IritaH -tA -taM, visfzwaH -zwA -zwaM.
HURLER , s. kzepakaH, kzeptA m. (ptf), asitA m. (tf), prAsakaH.
HURLING (subs.): a game: perh. kandukakzepaH.
HURLING , s. kzepaRaM, asanaM, pAtanaM; ‘of stones,’ SilApraharaRaM.
HURLY-BURLY: tumulam: v. Tumult, confusion.
HURLY-BURLY , s. kolAhalaH, halahalASabdaH, kAlakIlaH -lakaH, tumulaM.
Hurly-burly, s. tumulaM, kolAhalaH, tumula-ravaH, kalakalaH.
HURRA, HURRAH: jayaDvaniH. and sim, comp.s.
Hurrah, interj. jaya or harza-nisvanaH-SabdaH-nAdaH.
HURRAH , exclam. jayaSabdaH, praSaMsASabdaH, AnandaSabdaH.
Hurricane, s. prakaMpanaH, mahAvAtaH, ativAtaH, praBaMjanaH, vAtyA, pracaMqavAtaH, vegAnilaH, vAtAlI, vAtyAvegaH, cakravAtaH, javAnilaH, JaMJAvAtaH (with showers).
HURRICANE: (1) BkazBkA,-nilaH. and sim. comp.s., a violent h. blew: mahAbalo BazkBkAvAto vavO, Mah. i. 149. 2.;(2) praBaYjanaH, H.;(3) caRqavAtaH, javAnilaH, etc. (any strong gale).

HURRICANE , s. cakravAtaH, praBaYjanaH, utpAtavAtaH, ativAtaH, vAtyA, vAtyA- vegaH, caRqavAtaH, pracaRqavAyuH m., vAtAlI, vAtarUzaH, vAtagulmaH, JaYJA- vAtaH, JaYJA, javAnilaH, BfmiH m., nirGAtaH, pavanAGAtaH.
HURRIED (adj.): (1) tvaritaH (tA, taM) (= hasty: q.v.);(2) tvarAviBrAnta (f. ntA) and sim. comp.s.
HURRIED , a. tvaritaH -tA -taM; ‘spoken fast,’ tvaritoditaH -tA -taM, nirastaH -stA -staM.
HURRIEDLY: (1) tvaritam: v. Hastily;(2) sasamBramam.
HURRIEDLY , adv. tvaritaM, satvaraM, drutaM, SIGraM, avilambitaM, saraBasaM.

Hurry, v. i. tvar 1 A, SIGraM gam 1 P, sa-saMBramaM gam. v. t. tvar c. (tvarayati). 2 satvaraM Akfz 1 P or praRud 6 P, or prer c.; SIGraM saM-niH-pad c. or vi-DA 3 U or sAD 5 P. s. tvarA, saMBramaH, raBas n., raBasaH, vyagratA, vegaH, AkulatvaM, A-saM-vegaH, tvaritagati f.; ‘why are you in such a h(urry)’ kimasi saMBrAMteva (U. 3); ‘in a h(urry)’ saMBrAMta, vyA-kula, vyagra. [Hurri]ed, a. tvarita, SIGra; ‘a h(urried) speech’ nirastaM vacaH, tvaritoditaM. [Hurri]edly, adv. SIGraM, tvaritaM, satvaraM, sasaMBramaM, saraBasaM, vyagraM.
HURRY (v. i.): tvarate (tvar, c. 1.): v. To hasten.
HURRY (v. t.): tvarayati (c. of tvar): v. To Hasten.
HURRY (subs.): I Haste: q.v.: tvarA.II Bustle: samBramaH.
To HURRY , v. a. tvar (c. 10. tvarayati -yituM), santvar. — (Harry along, drive, impel) kfz (c. 1. karzati, krazwuM), samAkfz, prer (c. 10. -Ira- yati -yituM), praRud (c. 6. -Rudati -RottuM).
To HURRY , v. n. tvar (c. 1. tvarate -rituM), santvar, atitvar, SIGra (nom. SIGrAyate), satvaraM or SIGraM gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM) or car (c. 1. carati -rituM).

HURRY , s. tvarA, samBramaH, saMvegaH, AvegaH, vegaH, raBasaH, kziprakAritA, tvaritagatiH f., ASugamanaM, SIGratA. — (Bustle) samBramaH, AkulatvaM, vyagratA, vyastatA; ‘in a hurry,’ tvaritaH -tA -taM, samBramI -miRI -mi (n), samBrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, AkulaH -lA -laM.
HURRY-SKURRY (adv.): (1) astavyastam;(2) sasamBramam.
HURRY-SKURRY , adv. sasamBramaM, saraBasaM, sAvegaM vyAkulaM, samBrameRa.
HURRYING (subs.): “there was h. to and fro”: janA DAvanto'tastataH: v. Also haste.

Hurt, v. t. kzi 5 P, tud 6 P, hiMs 7 P, ard 1 P or c., bAD 1 A, vyaT c. (vyaTayati), druh 4 P, kzaR 8 P, pIq 10, apakf 8 U, vipra-kf, du 5 P; ‘does not h(urt) oneʼs reputation’ yaSaH na kziRoti (R. ii. 40). s. kzataM, hiMsA, apakAraH, apakfti f., bADA, pIqA, vyaTA. 2 apAyaH, kzayaH, hAni f., nASaH. [Hurt]ful, a. pIqAkara (rI f.), apAyAvaha, hiM-sAtmaka, bADaka, apakArin, ahita-hAni-kzati-kara. 2 hiMsra, GAtuka, SarAru. [Hurt]fully, adv. hiMsApUrvaM, sApakAraM. [Hurt]less, a. akzata. 2 ahiMsra, anapakArin, anupadravin.
HURT (subs.): (1) kzatam, causing of h. kzatadarSana, N.s.; vraRam (= wound: q.v.);(2) duHKam (= pain: q.v.), to cause h. without drawing blood: SoRitena vinA duHKamutpAdayati, V. s.

HURT (v. t.): (1) pIqayati (pIq, c. 10.): v. To [Page357] pain;(2) kziRoti (kzi, c. 5.): v. To injure; (3) tudati (tud, c. 6.), then the enemy h. (him) with sharp words: vAksAyakEraTa tutoda tadA vipakzaH, Si. xx. 77.;(4) by subs.

To HURT , v. a. hiMs (c. 7. hinasti, c. 1. hiMsati -situM), vihiMs, upa- hiMs, AhiMs, kzataM kf, kzatiM kf, kzaR (c. 8. kzaRoti -RituM), parikzaR, apakf, drohaM kf, ard (c. 10. ardayati -yituM), samard, pIq (c. 10. pIqa- yati -yituM), vyaT (c. 10. vyaTayati -yituM), riz (c. 1. rezati, c. 4. rizyati, rezituM, rezwuM), kzi (c. 5. kziRoti, c. 1. kzayati, kzetuM), han (c. 2. hanti -ntuM), vihan, upahan, tud (c. 6. tudati, tottuM), naS (c. 10. nASa- yati -yituM), duz (c. 10. dUzayati -yituM), druh (c. 4. druhyati, drogDuM); ‘you hurt me by your sharp words,’ tudasi me sarmmARi vAkSarEH.
HURT , s. kzataM, kzatiH f., parikzataM, hiMsA -sanaM, apakAraH, apakftaM, drohaH, aBidrohaH, apAyaH, kzayaH, upakzayaH, pIqA, vyaTA, AGAtaH, bADaH, nASaH, dozaH, viheWaH -WanaM, hAniH f., rizwaM.

HURT , p. p. kzataH -tA -taM, parikzataH -tA -taM, vikzataH -tA -taM, hiMsitaH -tA -taM, vihiMsitaH -tA -taM, apakftaH -tA -taM, kftApakAraH -rA -raM, arditaH [Page355-a+ 51] -tA -taM, pIqitaH -tA -taM, nipIqitaH -tA -taM, vyaTitaH -tA -taM, vihataH -tA -taM, dUzitaH -tA -taM, rizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
HURTER , s. kzatakArI m. (n), apakArI m., hiMsakaH, rezwA m. (zwf).
HURTFUL: (1) pIqAkaraH (rI, raM), h. thing: pIqAkaraM dravyam, V. s.;(2) hiMsra (f. snA) (not of things): v. Injurious, mischievous.

HURTFUL , a. hiMsraH -srA -sraM, hiMsAluH -luH -lu -lukaH -kA -kaM, hiMsAtmakaH -kA -kaM, apakArI -riRI -ri (n), apakArakaH -kA -kaM, ApakaraH -rI -raM, kzatikArI &c., kzatijanakaH -kA -kaM, ahitaH -tA -taM, nfSaMsaH -sA -saM, SarAruH -ruH -ru, SArukaH -kA -kaM, GAtukaH -kA -kaM, upaGAtakaH -kA -kaM, hAnijanakaH -kA -kaM, bADakaH -kA -kaM, sabADaH -DA -DaM, rizvaH -zvA -zvaM, anizwajanakaH -kA -kaM, drohI -hiRI -hi (n).
HURTFULLY , adv. hiMsApUrvvaM, hiMsayA, kzatapUrvvaM, sakzataM, hiMsraM, hiMsraprakAreRa, ahitaM, yaTA hiMsA kriyate taTA, yaTA kzataM jAyate taTA.
HURTFULNESS: (1) pIqAkaratA;(2) hiMsratA;(3) better by adj.
HURTFULNESS , s. hiMsratA -tvaM, hiMsAlutA, kzatikAritA, ahitatvaM.
Hurtle, v. i. saMGawwa 1 A, aBisaM-pat 1 P. 2 saraBasaM nizkram 1 U, 4 P or nirgam 1 P. 3 Echo, q. v.
HURTLE: saMGawwate (Gaww, c. 1.): v. To clash.
To HURTLE , v. a. samAhan (c. 2. -hanti -ntuM), parasparasamAGAtaM kf. — (Whirl) Bram (c. 10. Bramayati -yituM).
HURTLESS , a. ahiMsraH -srA -sraM, anapakArI -riRI -ri (n).

Husband, s. patiH, Bartf, upayaMtf, pariRetf, parigrahItf, vivoQf; kAMtaH, dayitaH, DavaH, nATaH, svAmin; izwaH, priyatamaH, prAReSaH, hfdayeSaH, all m. (poetical words); ‘h(usband) and wife’ daM(jaM)patI, jAyApatI, BAryApatI; ‘h(usband)ʼs brother’ devaraH, devf m., devalaH; ‘a second h(usband)’ diDizuH; ‘h(usband)ʼs sister’ nanAMdf; ‘h(usband)ʼs brotherʼs wife’ yAtf; ‘sisterʼs h(usband)’ SyAlaH, SyAlakaH, AvuttaH, BaginIpatiH. v. t. parimitaM vyay 10, (vyayayati), na vikzip 6 P, parimitavyayaM kf 8 U. 2 kfz 1 P, 6 U. [Husband]less, a. viDavA, anATA, patihInA, gata-BartfkA, nirRATA. [Husband]ry, s. kfzi f., kfzi-karman n., karzaRaM, kfzividyA, vESyavftti f., hala-Bfti f. 2 parimitavyayaH, gfhakarmanirvAhavidyA. Husbandman, s. kfza(zi)kaH, karzakaH, kfzIvalaH, kzetrikaH, hAlikaH; See Farmer. 2 vESyaH, viS m. UrujaH, UravyaH, aryaH, BUmispfS m.

HUSBAND (subs.): (1) patiH, get a h. who will not take to others: ananyaBAjaM patimApnuhi, Ku. iii. 63.; who had h. s and children: yAH patiputravatyaH, Ku. viii. 6.;(2) Bartf (m.), will choose a second h.: BartAraM dvitIyaM varayizyati, Mah.;(3) svAmin (m.), but you (are my) h.: kintu svAmI tvam, H.;(4) pariRetf (m.), Sa;(5) upayantf (m.), R.
HUSBAND (v.): vAhayati (c. of vahf): v. To use, till.

HUSBAND , s. (Man married to a woman) patiH m., BarttA m. (rttf), svAmI m. (n), varaH, voQA m. (Qf), vivoQA m., varayitA m. (tf), kAntaH, pariRetA m. (tf), pariRAyakaH, nATaH, dayitaH, izwaH, priyaH -yatamaH, DavaH, upayantA m. (ntf), parigrahItA m. (tf), kzetrikaH, hfdayeSaH, prAReSaH, jIviteSaH, prARanATaH, prARADinATaH, vettA m. (ttf); ‘husband and wife,’ dampatI m. du., jampatI m. du., BAryyApatI m. du., jAyApatI m. du.; ‘a husband's brother,’ devA m. (vf), devaH, devaraH, devalaH; ‘a second husband,’ diDizuH m. -zUH m. — (Economist) parimi- tavyayI m. (n), alzavyayI m. — (Cultivator) kfzakaH, kfzikArI m. (n).
To HUSBAND , v. a. (Economize) parimitavyayaM kf, na vyayIkf, na vikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM); ‘to husband one's time,’ na kAlakzepaM kf. — (Cultivate) kfz (c. 6. kfzati, krazwuM).
HUSBANDLESS , a. patihInA, BarttfhInA, BarttfrahitA, nirRATA, anATA.
HUSBANDLY , a. parimitavyayaH -yA -yaM, gfhavyApArABijYaH -jYA -jYaM.
HUSBANDMAN: kfzIvalaH: v. Agriculturist, farmer.

HUSBANDMAN , s. (Cultivator, farmer) kfzakaH, kfzikaH, karzakaH, kArzakaH, kArzikaH, kfzIbalaH, kzetrakarzakaH, kzetrikaH, kzetrI m. (n). kzetrAjIvaH, kfzijIvI m. (n), hAlikaH, kzetrapatiH m., kfzARaH, kI- nASaH, ArdDikaH. — (Man of the third tribe) vESyaH, viw m. (S), UrujaH, UravyaH, aryyaH, BUmispfk m. (S).
HUSBANDRY: (1) kfzikarman (m.), P.;(2) kfziH (= agriculture).

HUSBANDRY , s. (Agriculture) kfziH f., kArziH f., kfzikarmma n. (n), kfzividyA, anftaM, vESyakriyA, vESyavfttiH f., halaBftiH f., karzaRaM, kfzwiH f., pramftaM. — (Frugality, economy) parimitavyayaH, gfhakarmmanayaH, gfhaka- rmmanirvAhavidyA.
Hush, interj. tuzRIM Bava, SAMtaM, vAcaMyama-niHSabda a. Bava. v. i. Sam 4 P, pra-upa-Sam, tUzRIM BU, mOnIBU. v. t. Sam c. (Samayati), niBftaM samA-DA 3 U; See Conceal also.
HUSH (interj.): (1) SAntam;(2) tUzRIm: v. Silent.
HUSH , exclam. SAntaM, SAntaM SAntaM, SabdaM mA kuru, tUzRImBava, mOnIBava, niHSabdo Bava, vAca yama, vAgroDaM kuru, hUm, nIcEs.
To HUSH , v. a. Sam (c. 10. Samayati -yituM), praSam, upaSam, sAntv (c. 10. sAntvayati -yituM), SabdaSAntiM kf, SabdaroDaM kf, niHSabdIkf.
To HUSH , v. n. Sam (c. 4. SAmyati, SamituM), upaSam, praSam, prasad (c. 1. -sIdati -sattuM), SAntIBU, niHSabdIBU, mOnIBU, tUzRImBU.
HUSH UP: nigUhati, -te (gUh, c. 1.): v. To conceal.
HUSHED , p. p. SAntaH -ntA -ntaM, SamitaH -tA -taM, praSamitaH -tA -taM.

Husk, s. tuzaH, tvac f., koSaH, puwaH-waM, Ave-zwanaM. 2 buzaM-saM, kaqaMgaraH. v. t. nistuzayati-nistvacayati (D.), tvacaM hf 1 P, nistuzIkf 8 U. [Husk]ed, a. nistuza, tvaghIna. 2 satuza, tvagyukta. [Husk]y, a. satuza, tuzavat. 2 rUkza, karkaSa; ‘in h(usky) tones’ rUkzasvareRa, bAzpa-vfttikaluzaM.
HUSK (subs.): tuza (mn.), unbroken h.: aKaRqaM tuzam, D.
